grounding.quote:
A new observation may add obligations,
which join the known work, or invalidate a claim, which is re-established
or withdrawn before anything relies on it

The work state (§5) retains the unresolved outcome, the residuals and the
obligations still owed. A stop reaches no destination and discards none
of these

predicate.statement: Transitions compose only under refinement. Intake binds current state through exact subject/basis, destination or prerequisite through governed outcome, and preserved obligations through affected relations/invariants. Discovery can add obligations and enlarge known work; invalidated claims must be re-established or withdrawn before reliance. Obligations outside current attention remain open, and the next decision retains material dependencies on them. Authorised destination changes follow the owner and re-enter the owning relation; revised satisfaction proves nothing about former satisfaction. Completion requires sufficient evidence that current state satisfies applicable destination and acceptance conditions, with acceptance belonging to the decision owner; empty lists, counts and absence of recorded counterexamples do not establish it. Inability to continue causes an explicit cause-named stop: unavailable output takes non-candidate_ready availability; halting/out-of-authority ambiguity takes blocked/escalated; refused admission/activation creates no step. Stops retain outcome, residuals and debts. Progress uses outcome evidence, not remaining-item count. Intake and work state already carry the bindings; no further carrier is required.

grounding.quote:
Four findings from the empirical program constrain how the profile treats
Markov objects. They are working refinements: the program has produced
candidate evidence for them, not a formal closure, and the profile adopts
them as the best current reading of the construct (P3, P6;
rc.2 #four-working-refinements-indicated-by-the-empirical-program). They
are stated in the order and sense the pinned companion surface carries
(§13 Companion surfaces), each with the experiment that grounds it, so the
two can be checked against each other; where the companion later re-cuts
them, the pin fixes which reading this profile adopted (P6, P3).

1. Effective blanket is geometric, not set-theoretic (exp 17). A boundary
   stated as attribute-column membership leaks under bypass. The
   load-bearing structure is the identity axis, and a set-valued boundary
   over columns is an epistemic convenience rather than the object. The
   Representation law (§8) is read this way: the test is whether identity
   survives treatment, not which attributes are in the member set.
2. Attribute schemas sense and fragment; they do not isolate. Any fixed
   attribute basis partially aligns with a given object's identity and
   partially distributes it. Where a Markov-object overlay is published,
   it exposes the identity axis, not only the attribute profile. Schemas
   are evidence, not ontology.
3. Core identity, not core size, is the discriminator of objecthood (exps
   15, 16). A sparse invariant with semantically loaded content is a
   lawful object; a rich attribute cluster with nothing invariant under
   context variation is not. More columns do not buy more objecthood.
   This is why sparse first publication remains lawful under the
   Saturation law (§11).
4. Identity is a DC shift, not a principal-variance axis (exp 18). Object
   identity appears as a mean offset in representation space, not as the
   dominant-variance direction. Characterisation by "the biggest source of
   variance in the attribute set" systematically misses identity;
   characterise by typical offset from a null peer instead. This is the
   basis for excluding principal-component and maximum-variance
   constructions as identity directions (§10).

These refinements do not weaken the construct; they sharpen it into one
that can be operationally validated and reproduced in published overlays.
They constrain the construct and overlays built on it. They are not
admissibility conditions for entity cuts, which §9 governs (P3, P6).

predicate.statement: Candidate evidence supports the pinned working reading, not formal closure: exp17 favours a geometric identity axis and treatment survival over column membership; fixed schemas partly sense/distribute identity and published overlays expose the axis; exps15/16 distinguish invariant semantic identity from core size, permitting sparse identity but rejecting rich noninvariant clusters; exp18 identifies DC mean offset from null peers rather than principal variance, excluding PCA/maximum-variance identity extraction. Later companion recuts do not change the pinned reading.
predicate.uncertainty: The experiments themselves are not supplied or independently assessed.

grounding.quote:
Adopting this profile does not

a formally established conditional-independence object, for example
claims that a published Markov-object overlay is the blanket rather than
a candidate for it, are read as working commitments, open to revision
when the companion program produces a conditional-independence result
(P6, P5).

Promotion gate. The experimental result that would promote the construct
from candidate to established is a direction-native
conditional-independence test: given the identity projection, residual
variation along remaining components should be independent of the target
under plausible treatments. That test has been run and did not meet its
predicate, and its multi-layer successor did not either. The gate stands
where it is; it has not been met and is not relocated to accommodate the
negative result (P6).

This status attaches to the construct and to overlays built on it. A
published Markov-object overlay is a candidate-class overlay of a
candidate construct, not a certified blanket of a formally established
object. It does not attach to entity cuts: an entity cut is lawful
published truth on its own admissibility test (§9) and does not inherit
the construct's candidate status. A candidate entity that has not met
that test is a candidate; a published entity cut is not (P3, P6). The
status is inherited downstream: tooling that materialises Markov-object
overlays under this profile should default to a candidate-class
publication kind and reserve any formally closed publication kind for
cuts backed by a real promotion-gate result (P6).

grounding.quote:
If a Markov object is read as a
candidate identity-bearing cut, good software boundary design should
prefer:

- the smallest lawful carrier set that preserves the boundary's real
  authority;
- subordinate payloads staying subordinate unless they carry independent
  authority;
- resistance to boundary inflation, where many sensed fragments are
  promoted into peer objects without irreducible need;
- strongly typed semantic boundaries, so identity-bearing cuts are not
  left fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned.

This profile does not make the empirical Markov-object program a
prerequisite for all design work. The relation runs the other way: this
profile gives one theoretical framing for why these boundary disciplines
are sound, and DESIGN_MODULE gives the general engineering law that
remains valid even outside world-model products (P2, P6).

grounding.quote:

plain structural rewrite. Every treatment declares preserved structure,
changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity (P1, P4b;

rewrite step of
[ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement): what it preserves
and its licensing law are that section's, and a treatment that changes
meaning is an approximate step with its adequacy relation. The five

Fully qualified naming is mandatory. Many cross-domain failures are
preventable naming collisions. Fully qualified naming removes aliasing,
so the remaining hard work is real semantic transformation; IDENTITY §2
states the scoped identity it applies (P3, P1;
rc.2 #fully-qualified-naming-is-mandatory).

Value lists are domain artifacts too. Changing code sets,
classifications and value lists are governed temporal reference
artifacts, not static enum decorations (P3;
rc.2 #value-lists-are-domain-artifacts-too).

The world model sits above APIs and schemas. API contracts and schema
contracts are projections over the world model. They are useful because

authority (P6, P1; rc.2 #the-world-model-sits-above-apis-and-schemas).

Probability belongs in the epistemic overlay. The canonical published
entity cut should remain semantic and bounded. Probability belongs in

ontological identity of the published object itself (P3, P6;
rc.2 #probability-belongs-in-the-epistemic-overlay).

conditions: Every published entity cut; geometric details only where a declared representation space exists.
exceptions: Outside a representation space, discharge the boundary law semantically under entity-cut construction.

grounding.quote:
Every published entity cut is prompt-sufficient for reasoning (P3, P1;
rc.2 #representation-law). At minimum, the cut should make visible
identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and
ambiguity. "Make the effective blanket explicit" means: state the
boundary at which the entity's identity survives reinterpretation, not
enumerate a set of member attribute columns. Attribute schemas are
evidence for identity, not identity itself. The boundary is
interventional, not structural: the test is "does this identity survive
treatment across its adjacent domains?", never "which attributes are in
the member set?" (P3). Where a declared representation space exists, that
boundary takes its geometric form, the low-rank projection along which
identity is preserved under treatment, and a Markov-object overlay should
then expose both the distributed attribute evidence and the projection
that recovers identity from it. Outside such a space the same law is
discharged semantically under §9 (P3, P1).

grounding.quote:
`source -> tracing -> assurance -> attribute ledger -> entity cut`

The entity cut is the immutable projection, not the mutable source of
truth. "Projection" is literal: the cut selects one bounded identity and
boundary over the distributed evidence in the ledger, accompanied by that
evidence and the basis on which it was accepted; §9 states the
obligation, and §10 applies where the selection is expressed
geometrically in a declared representation space (P3). The attribute
ledger is the accepted semantic record over which the entity cut is
projected. A single ledger state can support many different cuts at
different identities, boundaries and context scopes; the cut records
which selection was taken, not that the ledger is the cut (P3, P1).

Every accepted object attribute should therefore be recoverable through
the object cut that contains it; the attribute-ledger entries that
justify it; the assurance basis that accepted those entries; and the
traced source surfaces that support the assurance. No object attribute
should exist without ledger support; no ledger entry should exist without
assurance; no assurance should exist without traceable source (P6, P4b).

Published domain artifacts should be versioned and explicitly superseded. The chain is source→tracing→assurance→ledger→cut. A cut selects bounded identity/boundary with evidence and acceptance basis; one ledger state may support multiple identities/boundaries/context cuts. Every accepted attribute should be recoverable through cut, ledger, assurance and traced source; none should lack the next supporting link.

grounding.quote:
Published world-model truth should be immutable per cut; reviewable by
diff; traceable to evidence; and superseded by explicit later cuts rather
than silently overwritten (P4b, P3; rc.2 #publication-law). The
filesystem and Git are sufficient for the publication plane in the
initial lane. A database, if introduced later, is a query-plane
complement rather than the constitutional publication authority. In other
words: Git is the publication ledger; a database is the query plane
(P6). This publication ledger is distinct from the attribute ledger: the
attribute ledger records qualified semantic claims over object identity,
and the publication ledger records immutable published cuts of domain
artifacts and object projections. Both should remain append-only and
replayable (P4b).

Publication and attribute ledgers remain distinct and both should be append-only/replayable. Git/filesystem suffice initially; a later database complements querying rather than replacing constitutional publication authority.

grounding.quote:
The attribute ledger is the immediate semantic source of an entity cut
(P4b, P6; rc.2 #attribute-ledger-law). Every entry should be a fully
qualified claim, potentially including a value or measured quantity; a
rule or constraint; a classification; a topology or relation claim;
provenance and authority information; and effective, observed and
publication coordinates. The ledger may be supported by one or more
evidence surfaces, including documents for declared semantics or policy,
code for derivation logic or invariants, and data for observed state or
emitted values. The profile does not assume one source per attribute; it
assumes one lawful claim record per accepted attribute fact (P6, P3).

grounding.quote:
Entities are recovered, not invented. A builder project constructs an
entity cut by trawling authoritative source surfaces for the boundaries
the operating model already commits to, then qualifying them into
published truth (P3, P6; rc.2 #entity-cut-construction-law).

predicate.statement: Recover rather than invent entities: inspect authoritative source surfaces for boundaries already committed by the operating model and qualify those into published truth.

conditions: Publication of an entity cut.
exceptions: Sparse, unique, historical, single-context, inaccessible or regulated entities remain publishable when the test holds with declared residual ambiguity/evidence limits.

grounding.quote:
An entity cut is admissible when its identity, boundary, authority,
state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity are explicit,
traceable, and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence
altitude proportional to the claim (P3, P6; rc.2 #admissibility). That is
the whole constitutional test. It binds what is true of a published cut;
it does not prescribe how a builder establishes it (P0).

"Explicit" admits three lawful values on every surface: a stated value,
stated absence, or stated non-applicability with its reason. A cut whose
entity has no adjacent-domain treatment says so; it does not manufacture
one. This keeps the predicate whole without adding evidence machinery
(P5).

Sparse first publication remains lawful. A unique, historical,
single-context, inaccessible or regulated entity is publishable when the
test above holds and its residual ambiguity is declared. Absence of a
comparison population, of repeated contexts, or of permission to
intervene is a bound on evidence altitude to be stated, not a bar to
publication (P5, P2).

predicate.statement: The whole constitutional test requires all eight surfaces explicit, traceable and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence altitude proportional to the claim, without prescribing establishment technique. Every surface may state a value, absence, or non-applicability with reason; do not manufacture treatments. Missing comparison populations, repeated contexts or intervention permission are stated evidence-altitude bounds, not automatic publication bars.

conditions: Interventional evidence preference applies where the builder can intervene.
exceptions: No listed discrimination technique is mandatory or exhaustive.

grounding.quote:
"Discriminated from plausible alternatives" means the cut states why
this boundary rather than a nearby one the operating model would treat
differently. The claim carries its own discrimination; a stronger claim
needs stronger discrimination (P3, P6; rc.2 #discrimination). Techniques
that serve this, none of them mandatory and none of them exhaustive:

- cross-context invariance: separate what holds wherever the entity
  appears from what a particular context adds, where multiple contexts
  exist;
- null-peer comparison: name a structurally similar entity the operating
  model treats differently, and state what separates them;
- adjoint round-trip: interpret the entity through an adjacent domain's
  treatment surface and back through its adjoint mapping, and show the
  identity claim survives;
- transplant: show what a neighbouring entity would have to acquire to be
  treated as this one;
- coat stripping: vary or remove contextual claims and show identity
  survives; vary an identity claim and show it does not.

The adjoint round-trip performs, at semantic altitude, the discrimination
the geometric boundary test performs in a representation space. Where a
builder can intervene, interventional evidence discriminates more
strongly than declarative evidence, and a cut should say which kind it
rests on (P6). Boundary is interventional in character, not structural.
A cut that states its boundary only as a set of source fields has made a
weaker claim than one that states the reinterpretations under which
identity survives, and should be read as such (P3, P1).

predicate.statement: State why this boundary rather than a nearby differently treated alternative; stronger claims need stronger discrimination. Optional techniques are multiple-context invariance, structurally similar null peers, identity-preserving adjoint round-trip, transplant prerequisites and coat stripping versus identity-claim variation. Semantic adjoint round-trip corresponds to geometric boundary testing. Interventions discriminate more strongly where possible; cuts should identify evidence kind. A source-field-only boundary is a weaker claim than treatment-survival and should be read accordingly.

A published entity cut makes the eight admissibility surfaces (identity,

or stated non-applicability, and records the basis on which identity was
discriminated (P3, P6; rc.2 #publication). Cuts are immutable: revising

(P4b). Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology are

survive and does not select the form they are stored in (P0, P2).

exceptions: Ordinary institutional recovery does not require this overlay law.

grounding.quote:
This law is the representation-substrate specialisation of §9. It
applies only where the builder operates over a declared representation
space in which identity is a geometric direction (a learned
representation, an embedding over ledger claims, or an equivalent metric
space); it is not required for ordinary institutional recovery (P3, P2;
rc.2 #markov-object-construction-law). Where it applies, a builder
project constructs the overlay by a directional, interventional
procedure. The steps below are both how the overlay is built and the
minimum structure that is stored when it is published. The declared
representation space is part of the overlay: an identity direction is
uninterpretable without the space it lives in, and directions computed in
different spaces do not compose (P3, P1).

conditions: Constructing a geometric overlay for a candidate object.

grounding.quote:
For a candidate object, assemble attribute-ledger evidence across context
variation together with evidence for at least one null peer (P3, P6;
rc.2 #1-paired-evidence-collection):

- multiple contexts in which the candidate is instantiated;
- a null-peer instance: a structurally similar thing that lacks the
  candidate's identity content, observed in the same contexts;
- paired ledger entries covering `(candidate, context)` and
  `(null, context)`, so identity-carrying signal can be separated from
  context-carrying signal.

The paired evidence is the raw material of the cut. The ledger entries
remain distributed; they are not the object (P3).

conditions: Accepting a candidate direction or publishing its overlay.
exceptions: A lawful underlying entity cut remains publishable without the overlay.

grounding.quote:
A candidate identity direction is accepted only if projection along it
preserves object identity under held-out treatments. The builder records
at least one acceptable verification (P6, P3;
rc.2 #3-verification-by-treatment):

- α-sweep: apply `x − α · d` on held-out contexts, and show the expected
  identity shift and its saturation behaviour;
- transplant: apply `x + α · d` to null-peer instances, and show identity
  acquisition;
- boundary test: overwrite attributes outside the projection support and
  show identity survives (this is what discriminates a geometric blanket
  from a set-membership blanket).

A direction that has no acceptable verification is a candidate, not an
accepted overlay. Publishing an unverified direction violates the
Representation law (§8). The underlying entity cut remains lawful and
publishable without the overlay (P6, P3). The empirical program that
motivates these treatments reports that the strongest of them,
direction-native conditional independence, has been tested and does not
close. Passing this battery establishes that a direction is verified for
publication under this profile; it does not establish a formally closed
Markov blanket (§4 Epistemic status) (P6).

Without acceptable verification the direction stays candidate and publication violates Representation law. Passing verifies publication fitness, not formal Markov closure; the reported conditional-independence test did not close.

conditions: Candidates appear in multiple contexts.

grounding.quote:
For candidates that appear in multiple contexts, decompose the attribute
evidence into an invariant core, the attributes whose contribution to the
identity direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts, and a context
coat, the attributes selected by the specific context, carrying
contextual reinterpretation rather than identity per se (P3;
rc.2 #4-core-and-coat-decomposition). Both are evidence. The core carries
identity; the coat carries treatment. The coat to core ratio is a
characterisation, not a quality metric (P3, P1).

predicate.uncertainty: N and the quantitative meaning of stable are not further specified in this section.

conditions: Before publication of the accepted Markov-object representation.
exceptions: Core size overlapping null-peer ranges is expected and acceptable; size is not diagnostic.

grounding.quote:
Before publication, discriminate an accepted Markov object from an
incidental attribute cluster by null-peer comparison (P3, P6;
rc.2 #5-null-peer-discrimination):

- is the candidate's core size in a range that null peers also hit? Yes
  is expected and acceptable; size is not diagnostic;
- are the identity-loaded attributes in the core unique to the candidate
  among its null peers? They should be;
- does the candidate's identity direction transfer more cleanly than a
  random diagonal in the representation? It should.

Failure on the uniqueness and transfer tests means the cluster is not yet
a lawful Markov object, even if its invariants are internally consistent
(P3, P5).

The result mapping later makes either failed uniqueness or failed transfer a not-yet-lawful result, even with internally consistent invariants; overlapping core size alone is acceptable.

Overlays are immutable: revised directions/new evidence/contexts/refitted space create superseding overlays. exceptions: Sparse first publication remains lawful under admissibility.

grounding.quote:
World-model construction is iterative. Builder projects may work a
bounded source-object set repeatedly until the resulting attribute ledger
is judged sufficiently saturated for publication (P2, P5;
rc.2 #saturation-law). Sufficient saturation means: materially important
attributes have traceable support; remaining gaps are explicit
ambiguities rather than silent misses; and the resulting object cut is
stable enough to publish and supersede later if needed. Sparse first
publication remains lawful (§9 Admissibility); silent unsupported
attribute creation does not (P5, P6).

Sufficiency means traceable materially important attributes, explicit remaining ambiguities rather than silent misses, and a cut stable enough to publish/supersede. Silent unsupported attribute creation is unlawful.

exceptions: Detailed mesh topology may remain product-local while the line develops.

grounding.quote:
Do not build one central monolith first. Build local published domain
artifacts and their entity cuts, then stitch them (P4a, P6;
rc.2 #composition-law). Composition preserves fragment authority,
bounded-context meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and
ambiguity. Higher-order models are composed from published domain
artifacts; they do not erase them (P4a, P4b). The preferred end state is
a federated world-model mesh rather than a single flattened enterprise
model. Detailed mesh topology may remain product-local while the line is
still being developed; profile-level mesh law should be ratified only
once the reusable node and edge model is stable (P2, P6).

Preserve fragment authority, bounded-context meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and ambiguity; higher-order models do not erase constituents. Prefer a federated mesh; profile mesh law should be ratified only after reusable node/edge structure stabilises.

conditions: Temporal-reference traceability applies where applicable.

grounding.quote:
Projection is downstream convenience, not semantic authority; the
semantic kernel remains primary (P6, P1; rc.2 #projection-law). All
projections should remain traceable back to governing objects; evidence;
treatments; covariance edges; adjoint mappings; and temporal reference
artifacts where applicable. Tables, schemas, APIs, mapping documents and
covariant transforms are all publication forms over the same semantic
kernel (P1). Because an API usually carries more business semantics than
a bare schema, the preferred structural order is
`world model -> API contract -> schema contract`. Query and traversal are
also downstream-facing conveniences in this sense: they may be a
first-class delivery pillar without becoming the constitutional core of
this profile (P6, P2).

All should trace to governing objects, evidence, treatments, covariance, adjoints and applicable temporal references. Tables/schemas/APIs/mapping documents/covariant transforms share that kernel. LLMs and other probabilistic systems belong primarily on the semantic
control plane. They should help with comprehension, candidate alignment,
ambiguity reduction and correspondence ranking. They should not be the
row-by-row execution engine for large-scale data movement when the
semantic understanding has already been accepted and can be compiled
(P0, P2).

conditions: Compilation demonstration is recommended where the line is sufficiently mature.

grounding.quote:
Adoption should not depend on winning the standardisation argument first
(P2; rc.2 #proof-law). Preferred wedge:

1. comprehend one bounded source slice;
2. publish one fragment;
3. stitch one adjacent fragment;
4. answer one painful question the incumbent pipeline cannot answer
   cleanly;
5. emit both conventional and covariant outputs side by side.

This is incremental semantic capture, not a demand for immediate central
convergence. The proof obligation is practical: build the world model
once, then show that the same semantic substrate can emit the legacy
artifacts the organisation expects and the richer covariant outputs the
profile makes possible. Where the line is mature enough, the proof should
also show that accepted semantic understanding can be compiled into
deterministic executable pipelines without losing the traceability and
challengeability of the governing world model (P2, P6).

Prefer a five-step wedge: comprehend one bounded slice, publish one fragment, stitch one neighbour, answer one difficult incumbent question, emit conventional/covariant outputs together. The practical obligation demonstrates both legacy and richer outputs from one built semantic substrate, without demanding immediate central convergence. Mature lines should additionally demonstrate deterministic compilation retaining traceability and challengeability.

conditions: Choose normative application specifications for primarily interaction/workflow/non-domain/extra-domain operational-policy problems; choose world-model substrate for interfaces mainly over stable domain reality.
exceptions: Simpler lines may use world model→application projections→implementation.

grounding.quote:
The profile stands in parallel with spec-driven development.
Specifications are usually normative; world models are usually
descriptive. A sufficiently well-formed world model can therefore project
large parts of an application surface without requiring duplicated
semantic re-authoring downstream (P2, P1;
rc.2 #world-model-driven-development). Preferred relationship:

`world model -> epistemic correspondence overlay -> deterministic compiled artifacts -> implementation`

For simpler lines the shorter compression still holds:
`world model -> application projections -> implementation`. Use
normative application specs where the problem is primarily user
interaction, workflow choice, non-domain behaviour, or operational policy
beyond the domain semantics themselves. Use the world model as the
semantic substrate wherever the software is mainly an interface over
stable domain reality (P2, P1).

conditions: Cut admissibility is evaluated at the cut's claimed evidence altitude.
exceptions: Declared absence/non-applicability with reason is a lawful surface value, not a nonsatisfied result.

grounding.quote:
| cut admissibility | `cut_admissible` | satisfied | each surface is a stated value, a stated absence or a stated non-applicability with its reason, is traced, and is discriminated at the stated altitude; a stated bound on evidence altitude with its residual ambiguity declared meets the test (sparse first publication) |
| cut admissibility | `cut_inadmissible` | falsified | a surface is neither a stated value, a stated absence nor a stated non-applicability, or is untraceable, or the admissible evidence shows the boundary undiscriminated from a plausible alternative; that surface or alternative is the counterexample |

grounding.quote:
Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value
directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):
`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,
naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim
needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and
`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground
other than `representation_space_invalid` (P5).

A verification not run. Where no ground of `extraction_inadmissible` or
`representation_space_invalid` holds, a candidate direction whose
verification has not been run has no result for direction acceptance:
the verification is the evaluation of that predicate, and it was not
performed, so it has no
closed result and is never mapped to
`indeterminate` or to any other core value
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed). The
direction stays a candidate (§10 Verification by treatment). In every
conjunction over its acceptance, the unrun verification is a planned
assessment without a closed result
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Gaps) where the verification was planned; where none was planned, the
obligation it would have discharged is uncovered coverage. A step whose output needed that verification and that stopped
without it ends `incomplete`, which
[ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
maps for the predicate "a candidate is available", never to
`indeterminate`; the step's work state carries the unrun verification as
a residual ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)).
Publishing the unverified direction is `published_unverified` (P5, P6).

Two readings keep the mapping total without coercion (P5, P1). A stated
absence or stated non-applicability on an admissibility surface is a
lawful surface value, not a non-satisfied result. Candidate-class and
established are standings of the construct, the first being FOUNDATIONS
§5's hypothesis standing, and candidate-class and formally closed are
publication kinds; none of them is a result, and a gate run that fails
does not falsify the construct.

Planned-but-unrun is a conjunction gap; unplanned is uncovered coverage. A dependent construction step stopping without it ends incomplete for the distinct candidate-availability predicate and carries the unrun test as work-state residual. Publishing it is nevertheless published_unverified. Lawful absent/inapplicable surface values, construct standings and publication kinds are not evaluation results; failed gate runs do not falsify the construct.

constitutional member set of the selectable STDO Product. The release may
also carry subordinate executable and interaction tooling (P6, P3;
provenance rc.2 README #standards-library). A cut carries (P3, P2):

- the carrier-neutral [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md), whose
  a_c theory stays separate from interpreted subject models and carrier
  encodings ([AC-020](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation));

  one closed model-family signature under an exact a_c basis without
  changing the calculus or selecting a consumer, and whose adoption stays
  optional;
- derived application profiles such as
  [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md);
- the companion guides [POSTING_GUIDE](POSTING_GUIDE.md) and
  [WRITING_GUIDE](WRITING_GUIDE.md);
- the non-deciding semantic locator index [GLOSSARY](GLOSSARY.md), whose

- compact read models for activations that need a compact method basis;
  their carrier awaits the ruling on the rc.2 compression rows;

  layout-neutral product definition overlay and the deterministic
  installed-release manifest; and
- starter templates under `templates/`: the single per-product product
  definition template, project specification templates, the project
  reference-frame basis template and agent bootstrap templates.

shared versioned store and resolves logical release URIs, so a product
definition names its basis by logical URI and manifest digest and carries
no machine-local path

and verified; it is not the default
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#12-bootstrap)) (P6, P3).

([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager),
[RELEASE §3](RELEASE.md#exact-cut-qualification)) (P3, P6). Neither the
mutable authoring head nor the moving version-line selector silently
replaces that consumer basis
([RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption)) (P6, P3).

grounding.quote:
A derived surface is material derived from owning
sources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame
for a task; it names its sources and owns no determination.

Matching source identities establish only that the surface was derived
  from those sources. They establish neither its fidelity to them nor its
  sufficiency for a question

value.label: Derived surface

value.definition: A rendered contract over typed authority, projecting the material selected through acquisition; it is not source law.

grounding.quote:
A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;
it is not source law.

value.label: Prompt contract

value.definition: Each performed evaluation returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome; an unperformed evaluation has no result. Five distinct refinements answer whether a step may begin, whether a candidate is available, whether a candidate is accepted at its declared boundary, whether an ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis, and whether an intended external effect occurred.

grounding.quote:
each evaluation it
performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
and an evaluation it did not perform has no result.

value.label: Step results and five refinements

value.definition: For the predicate 'the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis': activated maps to satisfied when contract admission has evidence, Z/R/required-edge semantics/basis/scope are exact, closure is finite and unique, projection supplies selected context and frame activation returns activated_frame; admission_refused(authority) maps to out_of_frame for unadmitted work authority or unavailable/unauthorised durable evidence surface and names the missing authority or surface and owner; admission_refused(basis) maps to invalid_basis when the cited outcome/prerequisite/experiment or named subject/basis cannot support the contract; closure_unresolved maps to invalid_basis for inexact closure inputs, nonfinite/nonunique closure or projection gap/refusal and names failed condition and basis coordinates; out_of_frame maps to out_of_frame for an undeclared required relation/capability in all available frame/actor pairings or no fitting context option; activation_refusal retains the cause-specific mapping owned by REFERENCE_FRAME §5.

grounding.quote: | `activated` | the contract is admitted with its admission evidence (§1), Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis and the scope are exact and the material closure is finite and unique (§2, step 1), its projection returns a selected context (§2, step 2), and activation returns `activated_frame` | satisfied |

value.label: Admission and activation outcomes

conditions: Lawful activation occurred.
value.definition: Availability of a constructing step's exact constructed candidate or an assessing step's closed results. For 'a candidate is available': candidate_ready → satisfied when exact candidate and transition evidence exist; refused → falsified when a governing prohibition or owner-valid construction refusal defeats construction, with that prohibition/refusal as counterexample; incomplete → falsified when the step stops without output because a needed evaluation was unperformed or undecidable on admissible evidence, or bounded execution ended first, with stop basis and residuals naming which; re_entry_requested(authority) → out_of_frame for a needed decision outside grant, naming its owner; re_entry_requested(basis) → invalid_basis when activated basis no longer supports work.

grounding.quote:
| `candidate_ready` | satisfied | an exact candidate and its transition evidence are available |
| `refused` | falsified | lawful activation occurred, and a governing prohibition or an owner-valid construction refusal defeats the requested construction; the prohibition or refusal is the counterexample |
| `incomplete` | falsified | the lawfully activated step stopped without its output, because an evaluation the output needs was not performed or could not be decided on the admissible evidence, or bounded execution ended first; the stop basis is the counterexample, and it and the residuals name which |
| `re_entry_requested(authority)` | out_of_frame | a material decision the step needs lies outside its grant; the value names the owner of that decision |
| `re_entry_requested(basis)` | invalid_basis | the activated basis can no longer support the work |

value.label: Construction availability

conditions: A decision owner disposes an assessed candidate.
value.definition: Acceptance result, distinct from and consuming availability and assessment. For 'the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary': accept → satisfied when the candidate closes its cone and preserves every affected governing relation; local_repair → falsified for locally defective implementation or proof with coherent governing relation; re_enter → invalid_basis when governing outcome, requirement, identity, lifecycle, authority, public contract or accepted design must change; reject → falsified for a violated governing relation or undisposed competing truth path. Assessor recommendations are evidence, never dispositions.

grounding.quote:
| `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
| `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |
| `re_enter` | the governing outcome, a requirement, an identity, a lifecycle, an authority, a public contract or the accepted design must change | invalid_basis |
| `reject` | the candidate violates a governing relation or leaves an undisposed competing truth path | falsified |

value.label: Candidate disposition

conditions: An ambiguity is declared.
value.definition: For 'the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis': resolved → satisfied for a recorded decision under policy permitting lawful probabilistic processing or human adjudication; carried → falsified when policy permits continuation with known open ambiguity, retained as residual naming resolving evidence/decision; escalated → out_of_frame when policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human authority the step lacks, naming that authority; blocked → falsified when policy or hard stop halts at the known open ambiguity, naming the halting condition and what lifts it.

grounding.quote:
| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |

value.label: Ambiguity outcome

conditions: An effectful step has an intended external effect.
value.definition: For 'the intended effect occurred', meaning its declared outcome is attained: completed → satisfied only when subject evidence establishes full occurrence and that the effect ended; not_effected → falsified when subject evidence establishes the outcome is unattained and no later completion can attain it, naming any part that occurred; completion_unknown → indeterminate when neither is established, including lost response without counterexample or full apparent occurrence while the effect may still act. Unknown outcome records the observation that would decide it. Ending is a separate question: evidence must establish the effect no longer acts or never began. Uncertain completion includes completion_unknown and not_effected with unestablished end.

grounding.quote: | `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |

An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
established.

value.label: External effect outcome and end

value.definition: Total handling declares next moves for every admitted condition class, including an explicit unknown class, without claiming universal condition recognition, provider termination or request completion. Hard stops override ambiguity risk appetite. Reconfiguration is cause-directed response to out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or incompatible results.

grounding.quote:
Each admitted condition class has a declared
next move, including an explicit unknown class. Total handling does not
claim that every external condition is recognised, that an invoked provider
terminates, or that every request can be completed.

value.label: Totality, hard stops and reconfiguration

value.definition: Refinement decomposes an outer transformation T: A → X into typed steps connecting success predicates P₀ … Pₙ. A rewrite replaces a representation, step or composite with another claimed to preserve meaning, including partition, regrouping, reordering, merging or substitution. Exact steps preserve meaning under the subject's declared interpretation; approximate steps require an adequacy relation and an argued composite end-to-end bound. A licensing law is an owner-declared law permitting a refinement or rewrite.

grounding.quote:
An outer transformation T: A → X with success predicates P₀ … Pₙ
is faithfully refined by steps Tᵢ when each admitted input satisfying Pᵢ
yields an output satisfying Pᵢ₊₁, retains every applicable invariant, exposes
other outcomes without coercion, and each output satisfies the next step's
declared domain and preconditions

A rewrite step replaces a representation, a step or
a composite by another that is claimed to keep its meaning, for example
by partitioning, regrouping, reordering, merging or substituting parts.

value.label: Refinement, rewrite and licensing

conditions: A material transition is being admitted.
value.definition: Each admission owner's independent derivation and validation of the complete enclosing relation from authoritative inputs. The relation includes every participant and equality join whose identity, validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by admission. Admission is one semantic commit of the complete transition on its exact authoritative basis, or none.

grounding.quote:
For a material transition, each admission owner is independently
responsible for deriving and validating the complete enclosing relation
from authoritative inputs

Admission
is one semantic commit of the complete transition, bound to its exact basis
identity; failure or interruption admits the complete transition or none,
never a subset.

value.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

conditions: Admission owners and supported boundaries are declared by accepted design.
value.definition: Qualification of the admission law for every such owner and boundary, with case applicability determined by supported input, state and operating or threat model. It covers direct and supported composite/nested forms, forgery, enclosing-relation ambiguity, stale/advanced and incoherent multi-owner bases, competing authority, reconstruction, exact replay and post-validation atomic publication failure.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of the admission law is instantiated for every admission
owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design

value.label: Standing structural qualification

value.definition: Persistent object comprising current workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with invalidators, residuals and known uncertainty over external effects. Carrier choice belongs to profile or realisation; resumption, checkpoints and progress accounting require no particular carrier. Resumption re-enters the same method over current material state, possibly with another actor. Acceptance checkpoints bind exactly accepted work; preservation checkpoints may retain unfinished or unaccepted work without acceptance, promotion or publication.
value.label: Work state, resumption and checkpoints

value.definition: Semantic categories: progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome; prerequisite work names the enabled obligation; preservation and repeated proof are evidence rather than new progress; rejected or superseded construction is churn; discovery of hidden distance revises forecast rather than creating negative progress. These categories are not a numerical progress algorithm.

grounding.quote:
Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
forecast and is not negative progress.

value.label: Progress, prerequisites, evidence, churn and forecast revision

value.definition: Source-authored foundation-to-law traces distinguish standing, instance premises, consequences, owner choices and consumers. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are independent; P4b derives from P0/P2 with the non-reacquirability premise for step-produced facts; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. Transition-family premises are a selected outcome with acceptance conditions, possibly multi-activation work, actors with declared capability envelopes, and an admitted grant. Work-state-family premises are persistent workspace, work spanning activations, actors that may change, and external effects in an open world. These are work conditions, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs,
not commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

Its instance premises are: (a) a workspace that
persists across activations; (b) work that spans activations; (c) actors
that may change between activations; (d) external effects in an open
world. They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

value.label: Foundation-to-law trace

value.definition: The persistent workspace and its authoritative inputs are the continuing truth surface: their current material state determines what work has occurred. An actor's context is a bounded, revisable and disposable projection, never another truth surface. Work state, workspace and closed results carry continuity without a further carrier.

grounding.quote:
An account is
never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
it

value.label: Workspace truth and actor account

value.definition: Proportionality relates semantic ambiguity removed to effective reasoning complexity introduced. Complexity includes independent concepts and authority surfaces, cross-document joins, exceptions, branches, states, transitions, reconciled duplicate representations and decision-relevant detail; it is not line count, artifact count or context-window size. Rival authority, failure-classification uncertainty and evidence uncertainty count only insofar as they leave materially different semantic, authority, outcome or acceptance interpretations, not as additional benefits.

grounding.quote:
Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and
effective reasoning complexity introduced.

value.label: Proportionality

conditions: A cost claim is the governed question.
value.definition: A selected cost claim has an activation-declared allowance and reported spend measured under its selected execution binding or explicitly unmeasured. Material startup, framework processing, external computation, transport and assurance costs are separate. Supported input dimensions and workloads precede qualification; transferred-context cost includes every delegated actor, not just the coordinator. Report volume differs from model traffic.

grounding.quote:
Cost is selected, not universal. Where a cost claim is the governed
question, the activation declares its allowance and reports its spend,
measured under the selected execution binding or recorded as unmeasured

value.label: Selected cost claim

value.definition: A resource limit bounds activation consumption of context, attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or machine resources. The subsection owns the generic declaration, measurement and observance law, not a numerical value. The selected execution binding sets values and measurable units and boundaries; SPEC_METHOD §11 supplies the referenced build-tenant binding.

grounding.quote:
A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value

value.label: Resource limit

value.definition: A closed result identifies its frame, activation, subject, basis, evaluation, actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. It supports handoff without private working context while preserving provenance, validity and independence conditions. A result is affected by a change when its dependencies D*(t) meet impact cover I(Δ). Invalidation withdraws direct reliance, not necessarily its evidence and not necessarily the truth of its claim.

grounding.quote:
A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
uncertainty and the invalidation conditions

value.label: Closed result

value.definition: The three invalidator kinds are material input change, changed bound basis coordinate, and occurrence of a revising observation declared by the result or judgment. Material input includes newly acquired or changed admissible evidence that could change the result's value. Changed source, task or actor conditions count as basis changes where bound, otherwise material input changes; a role change matters when it changes a required actor condition.
exceptions: Role, conversation or resumption change that changes none of these invalidates nothing.

grounding.quote:
- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.

value.label: Closed-result invalidator

value.definition: Transition evidence is a consumer-represented read model identifying exact candidate, affected relations, changed realisation paths, added or removed authority paths, retained and open seams, focused proof, required integration proof and explicit non-changes. If an assessor was activated it includes that assessor's recommended disposition; once the decision owner decides, the owner's disposition appears beside it.

grounding.quote:
Transition evidence is a read
model; it does not become specification, design or admission authority

value.label: Transition evidence

value.definition: The source-disposition ledger reports predecessor conservation, new successor material, ownership and proposed changes. It reports UP-020 and six subsections conserved across §§1,3,5,7, with generic work state, uncertain-effect reconciliation and non-idempotence new; workspace/account, family tables, transitions, configuration, effects, derived-surface staleness, refinement additions and resource-limit law new. It routes UP-018 to DESIGN_MODULE §7 and general reconstruction to Intake; probabilistic work boundary to FOUNDATIONS; RF engagement across §§1–4,7; AC-010/011 to AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS with §2 applying them with RF-002/003/004/014/017; RF-012/AC-007 and result conjunction to FOUNDATIONS §4; admission provenance to TICKETS with new core mappings; ambiguity outcomes and hard stops to §§3–4; ODD graph functions to generic typed refinement while ODD 11.8 remains profile law; UP-017 to DESIGN_MODULE §5 and local seam rules; UP-021 and standing structural qualification to §4; UP-014 to §6 with delivery priority in SPEC_METHOD §8, and UP-005/019 to DESIGN_MODULE; closed-result return and generic reuse to §7 and ticket continuity to TICKETS §7. These are source-authored disposition reports, not findings of conservation by this interpretation.

grounding.quote: a table decides nothing and names the rule that states each consequence.

value.label: ACTIVATION predecessor-disposition ledger

value.definition: ASSURANCE is the tier-2 owner of assurance and testing law: verification layers, test taxonomy and authority, fixture portability, scenarios, installed proof, significant paths, testing frames, combination coverage, path erasure, evidence composition, subject acquisition, localisation and interface integration. It consumes tier-1 FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, EVALUATION and ACTIVATION without adding tier-1 definitions. SPEC_METHOD supplies chain/change classes; PRODUCT_DEFINITION supplies project bindings. Design-profile module proof and TICKETS test-case authority retain their scopes. EXECUTIVE_BASELINE maps roles at tier 3 without being a dependency. The two predecessor anchor conventions are provenance only; the standalone successor claim says received rows are restated without requiring the predecessor cut.

grounding.quote: reuse); adds no definition to tier 1.

value.label: ASSURANCE member

value.definition: Requirements preserve invariant truth and ask what must be true; design preserves structural choice and asks how that truth is realised; scenarios preserve operational meaning and ask whether the realised system can do the claimed thing. Scenarios are concrete end-to-end use cases at the product-owner layer, validating intent through realised behaviour.

grounding.quote:
| Requirements | invariant truth | what must be true? |
| Design | structural choice | how is that truth realised? |
| Scenarios | operational meaning | can the realised system actually do the claimed thing? |

value.label: Distinct verification layers

conditions: The relevant instance premises apply; commitments alone do not supply them.
value.definition: F14 accounts for assurance §§1–16 and identifies evidence law, its stated foundation premises and added domain choices. Instance premises are executable/observable source and runnable product forms; modules, interfaces and owners composed along causal paths; user outcomes through supported surfaces; external workers, transports or fixtures; and optionally a design profile governing module ownership. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are independent where cited; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts. §17 is disposition recording, not decision authority.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises, which the commitments
do not supply, are named in the rows as follows: runnable product, a
product's realisation can be executed or observed, in a source form and in
a deployed, installed or otherwise runnable form, to produce evidence;

value.label: Assurance and testing foundation family

value.definition: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance under the selected complete STDO basis, proof authority has two primary sources: design/module conformance and constitutional user/Product acceptance. Conformance derives from governing design, module ownership, declared carrier inventory or equivalent, structural diagrams where present and boundary-local fail-closed law; unit tests belong here, and integration, negative or fail-closed tests may belong here when targeting a designed boundary. Acceptance derives from requirements, acceptance criteria, scenarios/use cases and Product release/qualification claims. Execution breadth, speed and live/deterministic mode do not determine authority.

grounding.quote:
Authority source is not execution breadth. A test may be small or broad,
fast or slow, deterministic or live, and still derives from one of two
primary authorities (P6, P1):

1. design or module conformance tests; and
2. UAT, or acceptance, tests.

value.label: Product test-authority taxonomy

value.definition: Sandbox UAT exercises a deployed, installed or otherwise runnable composed Product through declared application, public, runtime or control surfaces, driven by a requirement-sourced scenario or acceptance case. Harnessed mode uses deterministic, fake, recorded or injected external workers/results and proves exercised composition, orchestration, control, projection, archive and scenario wiring. Live mode crosses the real configured external worker/tool/agent/service/transport and returns evidence through declared result, evaluation, provenance and projection surfaces.

grounding.quote:
- harnessed sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a
  deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker or result surface; and
- live sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a real
  configured worker, tool, agent, service or other external probabilistic
  transport where the product depends on that live boundary.

value.label: Harnessed and live sandbox UAT

value.definition: Fixture portability concerns reproducibility of required closure lanes from a declared source boundary and explicit treatment of external project evidence. A missing fixture is a governed diagnostic naming fixture authority and lane, not a Product semantic failure.

grounding.quote:
A missing external fixture fails with a governed diagnostic that names the
fixture authority and the lane; it never masquerades as a product semantic
failure

value.label: Fixture and proof portability

value.definition: Written, traceable test-case authority includes appropriate scenario bundles, ordered sequences, negative/control cases or other explicit evidence cases. Each expected assertion carries its owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation, shared dependencies and whether its predicate is the obligation itself, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction.

grounding.quote:
Written authority includes the assertion
provenance of each expected result: the owning obligation, its
interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies, and
whether the asserted predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition of
it or part of a sufficient conjunction

value.label: Written test-case authority

value.definition: A scenario bundle exposes the feature/use-case boundary, coherent ordered test sequence and expected outcomes at each significant step. Declared scenarios pressure intent and design to name operational boundary, sequence, actors, controls and outcomes, and are described as the best source for identifying significant code/control paths.

grounding.quote:
A scenario bundle shows the feature or use-case boundary being exercised,
the test-case sequence that proves it, and the outcomes expected at each
significant step. It is the layer that makes operational meaning
inspectable

value.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.
value.definition: Installed-development proof is the decisive lane against an installed development version treated as an independent project or external target. Its recommended form uses a fresh sandbox or equivalent isolation, an installed/built development artifact and the real Product's declared entry, control and runtime surfaces.

grounding.quote:
Where a system has an installable or runnable development form, the
decisive proving lane runs against an installed development version as if
it were an independent project or an externalised target, not only against
the source tree in place

value.label: Installed development proof

value.definition: Significant path coverage intentionally names and proves meaningful paths for the claimed behaviour, not every branch in every file. Usual paths, where relevant, are intended success; fail-closed/rejection; boundary/control; integration/dispatch/transport; and recovery/retry/replay.

grounding.quote:
Exhaustive proof does not mean every possible branch in every file; it
means the project names the meaningful paths and proves them
intentionally. The significant paths usually include, where relevant:

value.label: Significant path coverage

value.definition: A testing frame executes or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim using an explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification condition. A file, suite, runner, fixture, scenario label, percentage or actor is not a frame merely by existing; counts, duration and framework category cannot enlarge its exercised claim.

grounding.quote:
A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes
or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an
explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification
condition.

value.label: Testing frame

value.definition: The authoritative Product path is the declared ordinary causal composition from supported user/public entry through exact selected interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery boundaries to the required outcome projection. Material combinatorial complexity is the claim-relative population of independent dimensions and interactions able to change outcomes, violate invariants, select another authority path or expose failure. Unit dimensions include module public-contract laws, operators, calculation regimes, states, transitions, boundary classes and failures; cross-participant, Product, persistence, configuration and user-role combinations belong at integration, end-to-end or user-acceptance boundaries.

grounding.quote:
An authoritative Product path is the declared ordinary causal composition
from a supported user or public entry, through the exact selected
interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery
boundaries, to the outcome projection the Product claim requires.

value.label: Authoritative Product path and its material combinations

conditions: Governing frame configuration or admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion, closure or release-assurance claim.
value.definition: The ordinary claim-relative testing set contains user acceptance for supported user outcome, end to end for complete runnable causal realisation, integration for one material composition boundary and interaction population, and unit for one module-owned law. It adds no role, stage, authority hierarchy or testing hierarchy. Claims, subjects, paths, populations, oracles and falsification boundaries select frames, not runners. Placement makes the set and §§8–13 available without adoption or activation.

grounding.quote:
Placement in this member makes the
set, and the law of §8 to §13 that serves it, available; it adopts nothing,
and each activation is decided by ACTIVATION §1 (Applicability).

value.label: Claim-relative Product testing frame set

value.definition: User acceptance asks whether a declared user with admitted capability/information can obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through supported ordinary surfaces. Its subject/basis binds exact runnable Product, current Product/requirement/UX/identity/policy/acceptance authority, user role, environment and harnessed/live mode. Its manifold covers goal, entries, permissions, inputs, configuration, dependencies/substitutions, visible state/output, refusal, recovery and acceptance interval. Coordinates distinguish Product/artifact/install, role/capability, configuration, dependency realisation/mode, data/workspace/invocation/time/outcome/scenario. Invariants include applicable outcomes, interface/identity/UX/safety/persistence/release law and referenced RF/EVALUATION laws. Evidence comprises supported requests/responses, projections, claimed durable effects, refusals, recovery, scenarios and exact subject/dependency identity. Capability must reproduce the user's access and distinguish hidden assistance. Result is one exact user-outcome core result with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual user populations and invalidators.

grounding.quote: Can a declared user, with the user's admitted capability and information, obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary Product surface?

value.label: User-acceptance frame

value.definition: End to end asks whether the exact runnable Product realises its outcome across every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary. Basis binds composition design, supported entry, selected owners/dependencies, ordinary configuration and Product claim. Manifold includes all causal producers/consumers, contracts, authority transitions, state/events/processes, retry/replay/recovery and rivals. Coordinates include artifact/installed tree, entry/operation, definition/owner, paths/edges, process/event prefix/state, configuration/dependency/result/replay/scenario. Invariants cover composition, exact subject/congruence, required path singularity and lifecycle/authority/persistence/release. Evidence includes ordinary invocation, semantic path/authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, transitions, outputs, claimed reconstruction, artifact identity and negative paths. Capability observes the complete path unchanged and reproduces material states/failures. Result binds exact end-to-end claim, exercised edges, unexercised paths, counterexamples and residual combinations.

grounding.quote: including every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary?

value.label: End-to-end frame

value.definition: Integration evaluates actual participants' joint contract at one declared material composition boundary across result-changing state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery combinations. Basis binds exact declaration, actual implementations or expressly admitted substitutes, governing Product/requirement/design law and population. Manifold includes both sides, carriers, pre/postconditions, ownership, ordering, state, retry/recovery, translation and rivals. Coordinates identify participants/versions, interface/carrier revisions, state/configuration/dependency, case/input/output/failure/evidence. Invariants include composition law, complete participant admission, applicable atomicity/reconstruction and exact assurance boundary. Evidence comprises actual exchanges, admitted carriers, transitions, verdicts, failures/retries/recovery, combinations and identities. Capability exercises the real seam, detects substitution and varies every material interaction dimension. Result binds exact integration claim, covered combinations, counterexamples, omissions and invalidators.

grounding.quote: Do the actual participants at one declared material composition boundary satisfy their joint contract across the combinations of state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery that can change the boundary result?

value.label: Integration frame

value.definition: Unit evaluates one exact module-owned law across material operators, calculation regimes, states, transitions, public/private boundary classes and failures. Basis binds exact module, accepted ontology/design, active carrier inventory, owned requirements/public contracts, implementation and independently derived module-bounded decidable oracle. Manifold includes public contracts, algebras, calculations, parsers, reducers, state machines, transitions, combinators, admission predicates, conservation/invariant/numerical/error relations. Coordinates identify module/implementation revision, law/operator family, state/input/boundary classes, expected relation, generated case/mutation/result. Evidence may be law-derived examples, equivalence classes, available finite exhaustive cases, generative/property cases, metamorphic relations, algebra/calculation oracles, boundaries and killed internal mutations. Capability distinguishes independent law-based oracles from implementation restatements. Result is confined to the exact law and module population with counterexamples, residual combinations and invalidators.

grounding.quote: Does one module-owned law hold across its material combinations of algebraic operator, calculation regime, state, transition, public or private boundary class, and failure case?

value.label: Unit frame

value.definition: Testing value is indexed by material combinations discriminated for an exact claim. Its minimum coordinates are claim/subject congruence; number/materiality of independent dimensions; covered interaction strength; authoritative-path exactness; oracle independence/precision; sensitivity to realistic faults/rivals/history; observability/reconstruction/reproducibility; and explicit residual combinations/invalidators. Unit value normally rises with internal closed-domain complexity; broader-frame value can be multiplicative through interacting boundary pre/postconditions, authority, state, configuration, failure and recovery. Common Product factors are user role/capability; operation/composition; selected definition/owner/implementation/dependency; lifecycle/persisted state; configuration/versions; process/continuation/retry/re-entry/recovery; success/refusal/malformed/partial-failure/rival-path cases; fresh process/replay/reconstruction/migration; and visible outcome/projection.

grounding.quote:
7. observability, reconstruction and reproducibility of the result; and
8. explicit residual combinations and invalidation conditions.

value.label: Combinatorial testing-value index

value.definition: Technical-debt erasure distinguishes two finite subject-relative graphs. Production closure covers exact runnable form/configuration and transitive imports, exports, packages, switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers, generated runtime artifacts, recovery and fresh-process reconstruction. Assurance/source closure covers source consumers, fixtures, proof scripts, generators, mutations and assurance tooling relied on for the claim.

grounding.quote:
A successor passing does not prove the predecessor removed. Technical-debt
erasure evaluates two distinct, finite, subject-relative graphs

value.label: Production and assurance closure

value.definition: Testing evidence composition preserves distinct claim-bound results from even one execution. Each result states its established predicate; a necessary-condition result does not establish the obligation, and conjunction sufficiency is a separate claim. Default responsibilities are user outcome, complete runnable path, material composition and module-owned law for the four respective frames.

grounding.quote:
Each bound result states which
predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not
establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim
of its own

value.label: Claim-bound testing evidence composition

value.definition: Assurance-subject acquisition and evaluation are distinct. Owner-issued Product/runtime/lifecycle/admission/replay/projection truth is acquired through exact runnable owner surfaces, validators, projections, receipts or reconstruction relations. Evaluation may then use an independent oracle derived from Product, requirement and accepted-design law; independence does not require a parallel implementation of owner runtime meaning.

grounding.quote:
Where a
claim depends on owner-issued Product, runtime, lifecycle, admission,
replay or projection truth, the testing frame acquires that truth through
the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or
reconstruction relation.

value.label: Owner-issued assurance subject

value.definition: Counterexample localisation identifies the earliest supported causal frontier: causally minimal violated owner relations or seam coordinates under the declared causal relation, not chronological/log order. Exactly one domain form travels with the core value for the predicate that evidence establishes earliest violated loci: unique locus → satisfied; jointly established incomparable earliest loci whose combined violation is necessary → satisfied; unresolved alternative frontiers → indeterminate with alternatives and deciding evidence; no support for a bounded frontier → indeterminate with needed evidence. Established joint cause differs from alternatives, and unique locus differs from joint set.

grounding.quote:
One unique violated locus and a jointly established set
map to `satisfied`. Unresolved alternative frontiers map to
`indeterminate`, naming the alternatives that further evidence must
decide between.

value.label: Counterexample localisation and result domain

conditions: Governing frame configuration or admitted work authority selects the composite.

Each seam binds domains, pre/postconditions, lifecycle/time, context, mutable subject, refusals and observations. Identities, revisions, units, cardinality, ordering, empty/null/default semantics and validity intervals stay distinct; equal shape/output establishes no equality of meaning, provenance or authority.

It adds no fifth testing type, role or
universal activation gate

These are representative source-contract discriminators: not an executed

value.definition: Derivation provenance contracts nine recurring commitments: scoped identity/authority conservation; bounded-context meaning and explicit cross-context relations; bounded probabilistic construction; delegation, exact candidates and construction/assessment separation; governed ambiguity, human adjudication and hard-stop separation; exact-basis evaluation, evidence/verdict separation and closed results; constitutional derivation/re-entry; finite closure, projection, residuals and capability fit; singular released authority. The calculus contracts recurring commitments the method already
establishes. In this corpus each is law in a member of this candidate, so
applying the calculus needs no predecessor clause; the rc.2 clause family
from which this edition derived each one is listed beside it as the
