value.definition: Material family F9's foundation-to-law table distinguishes premises, consequences, rule loci, added choices and their owners, and pillar references. Its instance premises are a finite record model of a governed symbolic system; exact-subject interpretation with separately identified subject, model and optional carrier; and predicates requiring mechanical decision, bounded probabilistic construction or human adjudication. The consumer list records applications of nineteen rule groups without granting consumers new decisions.

grounding.quote:
- (i) a governed symbolic system is represented by a finite model whose
  records stand for its objects, relations, constraints, residuals,
  traversals, transformations and judgments;
- (ii) a model is interpreted from an exact subject and may be encoded in
  a carrier, and subject, model and carrier are separately identified;
- (iii) some predicates over a model are decided mechanically, and others
  need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication.

value.label: F9 foundation-to-law map

value.definition: Sigma = (RecordKind, Sort, RelationKind, ConstraintKind, ResidualKind, FunctorKind, JudgmentKind, StopKind). Each member is a finite closed identity set for one model family. The eight fixed core families have identities under urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind: with suffixes semantic-object, typed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation and judgment.

grounding.quote:
Sigma = (
  RecordKind,
  Sort,
  RelationKind,
  ConstraintKind,
  ResidualKind,
  FunctorKind,
  JudgmentKind,
  StopKind
)

value.label: Closed calculus signature

value.definition: M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J), with exact basis b, closed identity universe I and finite populations of semantic objects, typed directed relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations and judgments respectively. Population_M maps each fixed core record kind to its population. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M.

grounding.quote:
where `I` is the closed identity universe; `O` the finite set of typed
semantic objects; `E` the finite set of typed directed relations; `C` the
finite set of constitutional constraints; `L` the finite set of declared
latitude records; `X` the finite set of residual uncertainty records; `V`
the finite set of traversal records; `T` the finite set of transformation
records; and `J` the finite set of judgment records.

value.label: Model and record populations

value.definition: SemanticObject has exactly id, sort, context, owner, scope, basis and value. id, sort, context, owner and basis are identities; scope is the closed governed domain; value is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or an exact-content reference. Its scoped identity uses id, owner and sort, with scope as boundary.

grounding.quote:
`id`, `sort`, `context`, `owner` and `basis` are identities. `scope` is
the closed governed domain. `value` is sort-defined carrier-neutral content
or a reference to exact content. A semantic object is an Object of
FOUNDATIONS §2 whose scoped identity is carried by `id`, `owner` and
`sort` and whose boundary is `scope`.

value.label: SemanticObject record

value.definition: TypedRelation has exactly id, kind, source, target, context, owner, scope, basis and qualifiers. Endpoints resolve to I; qualifiers form a closed kind-specific record for signature-required direction, cardinality, preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation and other relation semantics.

grounding.quote:
`source` and `target` resolve to members of `I`. `qualifiers` is the
closed kind-specific record declaring direction, cardinality,
preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics
required by the signature.

value.label: TypedRelation record

value.definition: Constraint has exactly id, kind, applies_to, predicate, context, owner, scope, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref and refusal. kind and judgment_kind each resolve one declared kind. Its owning signature defines predicate language and judgment; predicates not deterministically decidable state the required probabilistic or human judgment kind instead of claiming machine proof.

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves
one declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate
language and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not
deterministically decidable states the required probabilistic or human
judgment kind rather than pretending to be a machine proof

value.label: Constraint record

value.definition: Latitude is an explicit permission set inside a constraint boundary, with fields id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis and invalidation. Silence grants no latitude, and a latitude record grants no authority beyond its owner, scope, basis and invalidation law.

grounding.quote:
Silence is not latitude. Latitude grants no authority beyond its owner,
scope, basis and invalidation law

value.label: Latitude record

value.definition: Residual is first-class model uncertainty with fields id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry and invalidation. kind resolves a declared ResidualKind whose signature defines lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains; undeclared kinds or values refuse structural admission.

grounding.quote:
`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines
its lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation
domains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission
(P3).

value.label: Residual record

value.definition: The source's core result domain contains satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis. Constraint judgments and operation outcomes answer different named predicates. Missing assessments have no closed result. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis), with cause-sensitive mappings rather than a generic success/failure collapse.

grounding.quote:
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

value.label: Core results and operation stops

conditions: Model M, seed set Z and dependency relation family R are supplied.
value.definition: Material closure is closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q)). Least means least lawful record closure under R, not globally minimal prose, bytes, tokens, cost or cognitive effort.

grounding.quote: closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q))

value.label: Material closure

value.definition: Projection selects a model view without changing selected meaning: project(M, Z, R) -> (M_Z, Boundary_Z) | gap | refusal. M_Z contains Z's material closure; Boundary_Z records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. Projection is a reference, not a new semantic owner.

grounding.quote:
`M_Z` contains the material closure of `Z`, so a projection's `gap` or
`refusal` is that of the closure it contains or of the model it acts on:
`gap` or `refusal(basis)` (AC-007). `Boundary_Z` records excluded,
external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A
projection is not a new semantic owner.

value.label: Model projection

value.definition: An overlay adds explicit records to one or more declared populations of a basis model without mutating the basis. Override, disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation and translation require typed relations carrying exact authority, direction, scope, basis, preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation semantics.

grounding.quote:
An overlay adds explicit records to one or more declared `Population_M`
families of a basis model. It does not mutate the basis. Override,
disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation or translation exists only as
a typed relation with exact authority, direction, scope, basis,
preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation semantics

value.label: Model overlay

value.definition: A transformation is an operation-bearing specialisation of one exact traversal. Its fields are id, traversal, domain_model, codomain_model, context, owner, scope, basis, operation_authority, preconditions, preservation_relation, preserved, introduced, removed, external_preserved, external_introduced, external_removed, external_resolution_witnesses, residuals, evidence, provenance, stop_states, invalidation and re_entry. T[t](M_b, inputs) returns a proposed successor M_b_prime* or hold, gap or refusal.

grounding.quote:
A transformation is an operation-bearing specialisation of one exact
traversal record `v` (§5).

value.label: Transformation contract

value.definition: Judgment is a model record pointing to an unchanged subject, with fields id, kind, subject, subject_digest, context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance and decided_at. Promotion is a separate explicit relation between that unchanged subject and an admission or acceptance judgment.

grounding.quote:
Issuing a judgment does not transform, rewrite, reissue or rename its
subject. Promotion is an explicit relation between the unchanged subject
and its admission or acceptance judgment

value.label: Judgment record

value.definition: A traversal is a typed contract with id, domain, codomain, context, owner, scope, basis, preconditions, postconditions, authority, evidence, provenance and stop_states. Application F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v binds one exact traversal, one functor kind, typed input/result domains and a closed stop algebra. Same-spelled profile, runtime or realisation terms require an explicit owner-authorised binding.

grounding.quote:
The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority

value.label: Traversal contract

value.definition: The subject's F_D, F_P and F_H have identities urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d, :f-p and :f-h. F_D classifies deterministic evaluation/proof returning a judgment without doing the judged domain construction. F_P classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or proposal without inherent semantic, admission, acceptance or closure authority. F_H classifies explicit human adjudication under exact identity, grant, subject, basis and decision contract; human presence grants no ambient authority.

grounding.quote:
- `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared
  properties. It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain
  construction being judged (P6).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

value.label: Subject functor kinds

value.definition: Interpret_a_c(subject_basis, signature, interpretation_contract) produces M_subject* or hold, gap or refusal. The star denotes a proposed model without applicable semantic acceptance. The contract fixes calculus basis; exact subject identity, inventory and bytes or semantic addresses; signature and compatible extensions; mappings to all applicable populations; interpreter identity, capability, provenance and stops; structural evaluation; semantic selection/acceptance authority; and re-entry/invalidation rules.

grounding.quote:
The stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` take their core values under AC-007
by their causes. The trailing `*` marks a proposed model that has not
received the
applicable semantic acceptance judgment. The interpretation contract is
the Interpretation of FOUNDATIONS §2 made exact for one subject and one
signature.

value.label: Interpretation contract and proposed model

value.definition: The governed layers are a_c (pure calculus), a_c.X (exact subject X interpreted as a model), and a_c.X.C (that accepted model encoded in carrier C). They have separate identities and proof boundaries. Semantic acceptance J_X and carrier admission D_C are external judgments; admitted encoding evidence is the triple (G_C, J_X, D_C).

grounding.quote:
a_c       = the pure calculus
a_c.X     = subject X interpreted as a model of a_c
a_c.X.C   = that accepted model encoded in carrier C

value.label: Calculus, interpretation and encoding layers

value.definition: AxiomaticCalculusBasis is an external edition-identity record created after publication bytes exist. It contains kind stdo.axiomatic-calculus-basis, schema_version 1, the stable concept_identity, derivation_basis {release_uri, manifest_sha256, principle_refs}, and publication_basis {release_uri, manifest_sha256, member_uri, member_sha256}. It separates accepted predecessor derivation authority from the distinct immutable successor publication carrier.

The stable concept identity does not identify one immutable calculus
edition. An exact released calculus basis is an external record created
after the publication bytes exist. It keeps the predecessor authority from
which the edition was derived distinct from the successor carrier that
publishes it

value.label: Exact calculus edition identity

conditions: A declared subject and work boundary select seed set Z and dependency relation family R.
value.definition: A constraint surface is project(M_subject, Z, R) over material closure. It carries objects/meanings, constraints/dependencies, admissible traversals/transformations, required judgment outcomes, explicit latitude, retained authority, evidence/provenance/bases, residuals and boundary seams. Shared premises are single records; closure imposes neither tree shape nor execution order. The surface constrains work without prescribing internal strategy beyond obligations.

grounding.quote:
A constraint surface states, for a declared subject and work boundary,
the obligations and the permitted freedom of the work: its objects and
their meanings, the predicates and dependencies that bear on it, the
admissible operations, the required results, the authority, the evidence
and the conditions still unresolved. It constrains the work without
prescribing the worker's internal solution strategy beyond those
obligations

value.label: Task constraint surface

Routes are provenance only and do not validate these conservation claims.

Rows received by this member. Anchors are into rc.2

value.definition: Tier-2 CONFORMANCE owns qualification cases and a map from common discriminators to corpus sections, cases and logical-review checks. A discriminator is a situation whose expected distinction separates conforming from defective corpora. A case names subject, mechanism, independently specified expected distinction and status. Status records a designed fixture, fresh-constructor runs or independent assessment, not a result.

grounding.quote:
A case names its subject, the mechanism under test, the independently
specified expected distinction, and its status. A status names what
exists: a fixture designed, runs by a fresh constructor, or an assessment
by an independent assessor under EVALUATION §3 and §7. A status is a record

records one.

value.label: Conformance case and qualification map

value.definition: C-01 through C-12 are failure classes reported from construction using rc.2 and predecessors. Each names a detecting mechanism and expected distinction; every listed case has status not run. The descriptions are test specifications, not observed passes.

grounding.quote:
These are failure classes observed while building with the rc.2 method and
its predecessors, as reported in the common inputs. Each names the mechanism
that must catch it.

value.definition: Eight comparative-baseline trials: T-01 exceeds one actor's context cap, repeats with tighter caps and includes a coupled cannot-fit case; its first fixture was run twice and reviewed, and CASE-2 run twice but not assessed. T-02 starts from sufficient but ambiguous feature intent and is not run. T-03 joins two valid bounded results under one outer contract; T-04 combines an observed failure with a required unassessed obligation; their shared T-03-04 fixture was run twice but not assessed. T-05 pauses, clears context and resumes with another actor; its fixture was run twice but not assessed. T-06 revises a requirement after partial construction; T-07 supplies a structurally passing candidate with defective required behaviour; T-08 uses sourced decision analysis with uncertainty and stale evidence; these three are not run.

grounding.quote: | T-08 Broader process use | a sourced decision analysis with uncertainty and stale evidence | facts, assumptions, judgments and authority stay distinct; the result is independently assessable | not run |

R-02 withholds validator folklore, author memory and whole-corpus loading from the same task; R-01 variant V1 was run twice, without assessment.

grounding.quote: | R-02 No private knowledge | the same with validator folklore, author memory and whole-corpus loading withheld | the activation still succeeds or returns out_of_frame truthfully | fixture [R-01](../qualification/cases/R-01/CASE.md) variant V1 run twice; not assessed |

value.definition: CD-01 tests peer actors without a central coordinator, unfamiliar responsibility names, redistribution of an operation whose external effect has uncertain completion, and an installed release-building executive alongside them. CD-02 realises identical requirements in software and a mixed human/software process, including a faster proposal that merges independent assessments and replaces a required human decision. CD-03 resumes from a stale retained summary conflicting with the workspace, including an external effect and a disagreement whose resolution exceeds the actor's grant. All three are not run.

grounding.quote:
A case here is
named CD (common discriminator); the numbers in brackets are those of the
discriminators it exercises.

value.label: Actual-use common-discriminator cases

value.definition: AR-01 puts one weak necessary-condition assertion in each actual-use expectation set: a wrong decision can satisfy it. AR-02 puts one insufficient observation in each set, recording two admissible returns, one correct and one incorrect, indistinguishable at the observed point. AR-03 uses an expectation writer, task actors and grader from one model family, with writer and actors reading the same owning sections. AR-04 changes two owning sections and adds nine against dependent curated frames, hashed expectations, interpretation and conservation readings. AR-01 to AR-03 are not run; AR-04 was performed once by the author, whose retention claims await nonauthor readback.

grounding.quote:
The first three are exercised by the actual-use trial of
criterion 4 and are not run until the product owner selects it; the fourth
was performed once by the candidate's author.

value.definition: A logical-review check is a qualified reviewer's reasoned construction of a discriminator situation against the text, seeking its expected distinction, a counterexample or contradiction without running anything. Its output is an EVALUATION §4 review result; structural checks do not establish it and it supplies no actual-use evidence. Checks are named L with the discriminator number.

grounding.quote:
A logical-review check is a reviewer's reasoned reading: the reviewer
constructs a discriminator's situation against the text and finds whether
the text yields the expected distinction, or finds a counterexample or a

conditions: Required at boundaries selected by TICKETS UP-007 or additional governing-basis policy.

value.label: Technical triage and its distinct decision projections

conditions: Exists only after successful Worker activation.
value.definition: The Worker's closed output to its declared consumer, the Executive in the coordinated branch. Its five construction-availability values refine only 'a candidate is available': candidate_ready→satisfied; refused→falsified; incomplete→falsified; re_entry_requested(authority)→out_of_frame; re_entry_requested(basis)→invalid_basis. ACTIVATION §3 owns their grounds and total, exclusive mapping after lawful activation. These are carriers, not new semantic dispositions, assessments or acceptance.

grounding.quote:
The work-result values are the five values of construction availability,
the refinement that
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability) defines for the
predicate "a candidate is available". ACTIVATION §3 owns their grounds,
maps each to exactly one core value, and states that the mapping is total
and exclusive after lawful activation. In this profile they are carriers,
not new semantic dispositions, and none of them is an assessment or an
acceptance of the candidate (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).

value.label: Work result

conditions: Activation detects an applicable mismatch or refusal cause.
value.definition: An activation_refusal returns its cause and the core value assigned by REFERENCE_FRAME §5 to the assigning authority or declared result carrier. It creates no Worker activation, Worker evaluation or Worker result.

grounding.quote:
An `activation_refusal`, with the cause and
core value that
[REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions) gives it,
returns to the assigning authority or declared result carrier and creates
neither a Worker activation nor a Worker result.

value.label: Activation refusal

value.definition: The subject identity required by ACTIVATION §7 transition evidence and EVALUATION §3 traceability. Generic method qualification requires freezing its construction result before material reference exposure; otherwise an immutable identity or equivalent exact-subject relation stabilises it sufficiently for the assessment. No lifecycle state named frozen is created.

grounding.quote:
An exact candidate is the subject identity that the transition evidence of
ACTIVATION §7 and the traceability of EVALUATION §3 require. Where generic
method qualification applies (EVALUATION §7), its construction result is
frozen before material reference exposure as that clause requires.
Elsewhere this profile stabilises the review subject through an immutable
identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation sufficient for the claimed
assessment. The profile creates no new lifecycle state named `frozen` (P3,
P6; rc.2 #exact-candidate).

value.label: Exact candidate

conditions: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis adopts this profile.
value.definition: A projection consuming that basis and recording the selected profile mapping, exact outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions additional to the Product binding. It is neither a second frame basis nor a source of the authority projected.

grounding.quote:
A baseline-adoption projection consumes the Product-owned Project
Reference-Frame Basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7. Where that basis adopts
this profile, the projection records the selected profile mapping, exact
outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions
needed in addition to the Product binding (§16). It is not a second
frame-basis definition and mints none of the authority it projects (P6;
rc.2 #baseline-adoption-projection).

value.label: Baseline-adoption projection

value.definition: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects existing decisions and cites their material sources. Adoption of this profile and admission of a configuration are distinct relations. The basis is an object distinct from cited authorities and creates no local-axiom authority.

grounding.quote:
Two relations stay apart here. Adopting this profile for a Product is
the Product authority's act, recorded in its Project Reference-Frame Basis:
inclusion in a method cut makes the profile available, and only Product
authority adopts it
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)).
Admitting a frame configuration, this profile's executive configuration or
another, for the decisions it makes follows the rule of
[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), Admission of a
configuration: the smallest existing authority that owns each material
decision admits it, and admission creates no new authority over it.

value.label: Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis

value.definition: The Executive's finite frontier and closed-result-ledger cycle over every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis. Its conceptual U tracks unresolved evaluations and M a finite dependency-ready activation subset. The notation requires neither a scheduler nor a frame engine.

grounding.quote:
U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis

while U is non-empty:
  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results

value.label: Attention cycle

value.definition: A basis for one Product or an explicit directed Product chain. It distinguishes every mutable Source Project, current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and composition edge. Every Development Product role binds one exact underlying Install; every edge names source and target roles, governing authority/contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and invalidation.

grounding.quote:
A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source
Project, current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release
Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and
composition edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying
Install identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, its governing
authority and contracts, its lifecycle, its evidence boundary, its refusal
and its invalidation (P3, P6; rc.2 #product-chain-basis; the Product-role
map in the basis is PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7, the lineage objects FOUNDATIONS
§2).

value.label: Product-chain basis

conditions: Selected where bounded construction and delivery across successive tasks need separate attention.
value.definition: One lawful configuration allocating construction to Worker, specialised as Writer for documents and records, required assessment to Reviewer, and coordination to Executive within an existing admitted decision grant. It is neither the method's default nor a role inventory required for all work.
exceptions: Where one sufficient frame covers the task, direct entry applies.

grounding.quote:
The executive configuration is the configuration this profile describes,
in the sense of [ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration).
It allocates construction to the Worker frame, specialised as Writer for
documents and records; assessment, where it is required, to the Reviewer
frame; and coordination across tasks to the Executive frame, which disposes
within the decision grant existing authority admits (§5, §8 to §10). It is
one configuration, selected where it fits the task, not an inventory of
roles that all work needs. Existing authority selects it or another
configuration under §16, and a configuration with other frames, names or
topology is evaluated against its own task as ACTIVATION §1 Configuration
states, not by its distance from this one (P0, P2, P6).

value.label: Executive configuration

value.definition: This profile's selected delivery strategy: the smallest real runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through the selected composition, established early and widened in bounded increments, or extended/revalidated when already present. It trades later widening for early end-to-end composition feedback without claiming superiority over lawful strategies of other configurations.

grounding.quote:
The Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
the selected composition. The path is established early and widened in
bounded increments; where it already exists, the affected thread is extended
or revalidated. Increments are chosen for consequential uncertainty,
dependency and interface reach, and failure impact (P2; rc.2
#steel-thread-delivery; the generic sequencing heuristic is SPEC_METHOD §8).

value.label: Steel-thread delivery

value.definition: Product family: evaluates one exact current Product claim, outcome, boundary and lifecycle using current Intent, Product, requirements, acceptance meaning and Product coordinates. Product and requirement authority retain meaning and acceptance; output is bounded evaluation and evidence. Immediate falsifier: design, code, tests, predecessor behaviour or local convention changes Product meaning or substitutes its subject.

grounding.quote: Design, code, tests, a predecessor's behaviour or a local convention changes Product meaning or substitutes another Product subject.

value.label: Product evaluation family

value.definition: Product Composition family: evaluates one exact directed edge preserving Product roles, Product Definition/Release Cut/Product/Install identities, Development Product bindings, contracts, authority, lifecycle, evidence boundary and invalidation. Chains use bounded edge activations and declared conjunction. Each Product keeps its meaning; cited authorities/contracts own the edge; output is evaluation evidence only. Falsifiers include inferred edges from nesting, shared implementation/actors, imports, tool reachability, matching output or builder convenience; confusing builder and authored Product; or one node silently redefining another.

grounding.quote: A chain is evaluated through bounded edge activations and a declared conjunction.

value.label: Product Composition evaluation family

value.definition: Design family: evaluates whether accepted structural HOW satisfies material constitutional WHAT, closes required design relations and preserves owners across topology. Accepted design under Product/requirements owns structure. Output may identify satisfaction, contradiction or design re-entry gaps, never invent Product truth. Falsifiers: implementation precedent resolving open material design, design creating Product meaning, or undeclared material relations/competing structures.

grounding.quote: The frame may identify satisfaction, contradiction or a design re-entry gap; it cannot invent Product truth.

value.label: Design evaluation family

value.definition: Design Component family: evaluates a bounded component and direct causal dependency cone against parent contract, internal relations, sibling seams and required outputs. Accepted design owns only its bounded composition decision; parent, sibling, Product, requirement and runtime owners retain theirs. Falsifiers: omitted material far-side seam, absorbed parent/sibling decision, or local closure despite unresolved direct composition.

grounding.quote: The component omits a material far-side seam, absorbs a sibling or parent decision, or reports local closure while its direct composition is unresolved.

value.label: Design Component evaluation family

value.definition: Public Boundary family: evaluates a supported entry/exit's assigned validation, selection, transport, refusal and projection while preserving interior owners. Product, interface, identity, security and accepted design define it. Output is a closed boundary evaluation, not recreated interior semantics. Falsifiers: interpreting owner meaning, sequencing hidden domain decisions, exposing interior carriers as Product truth, or admitting unsupported paths.

grounding.quote: The frame evaluates the boundary result or refusal and returns only its closed evaluation; it does not recreate interior semantics.

value.label: Public Boundary evaluation family

value.definition: Entity family: evaluates exact identity, kind, lifecycle, owner, representation and effect regime of one semantic, artifact or runtime entity. Product, domain, identity, requirement and accepted-design authority define it; output is identity- and lifecycle-bound evaluation. Falsifiers: substituting filename, wrapper, ticket, object shape, cache or process instance for stable identity, or collapsing lifecycle coordinates.

grounding.quote: The frame returns an identity- and lifecycle-bound evaluation.

value.label: Entity evaluation family

value.definition: Operator family: evaluates one material operation as an irreducible declared relation over admitted domain, inputs, outputs, refusals, algebra, effects and lawful compositions. Product, requirements, accepted ontology/design and the named operation owner define it. Evaluation creates no additional executable plan. Falsifiers: treating an endpoint/function/class/command/file label as the semantic atom, hiding the operator in orchestration, or rebuilding generic mechanics as domain law.

grounding.quote: The frame evaluates it without creating another executable plan.

value.label: Operator evaluation family

value.definition: Owner family: evaluates preservation of an authority-bearing or semantic relation's owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle, refusal invariants and permitted delegation. Existing named authority owns the relation; output is authority-congruence evaluation only. Falsifiers: rival reconstruction of judgment, treating source authorship as authority transfer, or widening a grant through proxy, foundation, frame or actor.

grounding.quote: The frame may evaluate authority congruence only.

value.label: Owner evaluation family

value.definition: Effect family: evaluates an action's pure, observational, artifact or runtime effect regime, including material commit, failure, retry, recovery, compensation, admission and projection law. Applicable Product, requirement, design, artifact, runtime and admission owners retain decisions. Output is effect-bound result/evidence. Falsifiers: collapsed regimes, owner-bypassing mutation, compensation treated as semantic rollback, or a read becoming rival writable truth.

grounding.quote: The frame returns an effect-bound result and evidence.

value.label: Effect evaluation family

value.definition: Reuse/Foundation family: evaluates normalisation and comparison of a material generic capability/dependency against credible lawful foundations, retaining irreducible local remainder and authority-bearing roles. Design capability/foundation selection law and the existing trade-off owner govern selection; no semantic authority moves to the foundation. Falsifiers: incumbent/local preference without bounded comparison, reproducing richer lawful foundations, scoring unknowns favourably or assigning owner authority to reuse.

grounding.quote: The frame cannot move semantic authority to a foundation.

value.label: Reuse/Foundation evaluation family

value.definition: Install family: evaluates resolution and exercise of exact Product, release, artifact, dependencies, configuration and callable entry through the admitted installed coordinate independently of mutable-source convenience. Product, identity, release, dependency, packaging and accepted design define the subject. Output is installed identity, reachability and refusal evidence. Falsifiers: substituting source imports, ambient resolution, registries, fixtures, rebuilt artifacts or moving workspaces for the claimed installed subject.

grounding.quote: The frame returns installed identity, reachability and refusal evidence.

value.label: Install evaluation family

value.definition: Proof family: evaluates congruence of an exact claim's subject, basis, path, population, oracle, evidence, falsifier, residual boundary and invalidation. Claim owner keeps meaning; applicable testing, assurance, review, Product and release owners govern evaluation/acceptance. Output is evidence and closed evaluation, never Product meaning or disposition. Falsifiers: harness-recreated owner meaning, wrong subject/path, counts or aggregate green substituted for claims, or proof tooling mutating the subject undetectably.

grounding.quote: The frame returns evidence and a closed evaluation result, not Product meaning or disposition.

value.label: Proof evaluation family

value.definition: A claim whose value comes from its declared conjunction. Coverage is the union of admissible observations contributed by activated frames. Each material cross-frame seam is a mandatory result or required coverage preserving or lawfully translating exact identity, coordinate, basis, carried value/evidence, lifecycle scope, authority and provenance.

grounding.quote:
Coverage records the union of admissible observations the activated frames
contribute. A composite claim takes the value of its declared conjunction
under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Reported value. This profile's declared rule makes each material
cross-frame seam a mandatory result or required coverage: the seam
preserves, or lawfully translates, exact identity, coordinate and basis,
carried value or evidence, lifecycle scope, authority and provenance

value.label: Composite claim and seam coverage

conditions: The specialist set is adopted.
value.definition: ASSURANCE §7 user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration and unit testing frames supply claim-congruent evidence to Proof evaluations while retaining distinct claims and coordinates. The ASSURANCE §13 end-to-end interface integration frame relates Public Boundary, Design, Operator, Owner and Proof to integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames; its computational whole-path evaluation composes selected interface claims with Operator, Owner, Reuse/Foundation and Proof. Neither adds a thirteenth family, fifth testing type, role or universal activation gate.

grounding.quote:
The end-to-end interface integration frame (ASSURANCE §13) relates the
Public Boundary, Design, Operator, Owner and Proof families to the
integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames. Its computational
whole-path evaluation composes the selected interface claims with Operator,
Owner, Reuse/Foundation and Proof. Neither adds a thirteenth family, a fifth
testing type, a role or a universal activation gate (P2; rc.2
#derived-end-to-end-interface-integration-frame,
#computational-whole-path-evaluation).

value.label: Testing and interface frame relations

value.definition: Eight bounded communication projections: Worker activation, activation refusal, work result, Reviewer activation, review result, specialist activation, specialist result, and disposition/checkpoint. They carry exact intake/results and source routes between declared producers and consumers, without creating authority or implicit continuation.

grounding.quote:
The coordinated branch uses the following bounded projections. They may be
fields in existing Goals, tickets, design assets, commentary, qualification
or release evidence, or other admitted carriers; the profile requires no new
artifact type (P2, P6; rc.2 #handoff-projection).

value.label: Handoff projections

value.definition: A configuration defined by existing Product, requirement, Goals or accepted-design authority, potentially using different frames, names, overlaps, sequences and actor bindings. It is evaluated against its task, dependencies, actor limits, authority and required assurance, retaining every applicable method relation and identifying claim coverage.

grounding.quote:
A project configuration need not keep the labels Executive, Worker and
Reviewer or map one local frame to each. It keeps every applicable method
relation and identifies how its evaluations cover the claims it makes. It
is evaluated against its task, its dependencies, its actors' limits, the
authority it applies and the required assurance, as ACTIVATION §1
Configuration states, never by its labels, its topology or its difference
from this profile. A local axioms document may carry the accepted
configuration; its authority is the cited Goals, Product, requirement or
accepted-design decision, not the document's category (P6, P1).

value.label: Project-defined configuration

value.definition: The profile distinguishes actor identities from frame identities. Activation binds an actor to a frame; the profile specifies no actor count.

grounding.quote:
Frames and actors are separate identities: activation binds an actor to
a frame

value.label: Profile actor binding

value.definition: Qualification of the Executive baseline applies frame qualification and method self-qualification, creating no additional qualification protocol. A profile trial evaluates this profile and its declared composition with the exact REFERENCE_FRAME basis; neither is reproduced as peer authority.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of this profile applies frame qualification and method
self-qualification (EVALUATION §7); it creates no other qualification
protocol

value.label: Profile qualification

conditions: A Product adopts this baseline.
value.definition: Executive Baseline Adoption Additions is a template supplement to the adoption record owned by §16. It records exact profile identity; Executive, Worker and Reviewer declaration or acquisition references; role-specific capability, authority and independence bindings; Product severity and priority scales, current-boundary cutoff, non-waivable hard stops and triage relation; referenced ACTIVATION §3 work-to-core mapping and refinement mappings; twelve generic family declarations, non-material evidence or residuals; testing claims, topology, material combinations, scenario matrix, oracles and required/forbidden authoritative paths; profile activation-refusal, closed-result, conjunction and return relations; and qualification evidence and residuals.

grounding.quote: # Executive Baseline Adoption Additions

- work-result to core-result mapping: ACTIVATION §3 construction
  availability, recorded by reference, with each project refinement of a
  work-result value mapped to its parent value's core value (ACTIVATION §3):

value.label: Executive Baseline Adoption Additions

value.definition: Worker, Reviewer and Executive have distinct profile-specific activation additions to the generic minimal activation binding: execution intake and applicable operation grant for Worker; exact assessment and technical-triage coordinates for Reviewer; Product, mandate, frontier, ledgers, policy, conjunction and disposition grant for Executive.

grounding.quote:
Every activation first carries the generic binding of REFERENCE_FRAME §11
(minimal activation binding). This profile adds, by frame

value.label: Profile activation bindings

value.definition: The failure-classification table maps observations to a first diagnosis and routes evaluation. Its diagnoses are not predetermined verdicts.

grounding.quote: The table routes evaluation; it does not predetermine a verdict

value.label: Failure classification

value.definition: The anti-patterns identify thirty-two ways the Executive baseline is misapplied, spanning frame identity, authority, return topology, subject acquisition, evidence, testing, causal localisation and triage.

grounding.quote: The profile is misapplied when

Work-item closure applies the externally owned condition-based closure rule.

3. Executive, Worker and Reviewer are available finite evaluation frames,
   activated only where applicable, not a hierarchy or actor identities;

value.definition: The source-dispositions ledger records predecessor rc.2 STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md anchors, their stated conservation or proposed supersession, and destination loci. Routes are provenance only; conserved claims are said to be restated at their tenant loci, with ASSURANCE and EVALUATION destinations also listed in those members. Synthetic child anchors isolate proposed changed clauses.

Every conserved row is restated in tenant text at its locus; a route is
provenance only. Rows that land in ASSURANCE or EVALUATION are listed here
and in those members' tables.

value.label: Baseline source-dispositions ledger

value.definition: FOUNDATIONS is a Tier 1 member owning standing vocabulary; ontology, frame, authority, lineage and work-boundary objects; construction accounts and imports; P0–P6 commitments, foundation-to-law format and family index; composition, conservation, core results, conjunction and categorical demonstration requirements; and hypotheses.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns the vocabulary of standing (§1); the ontology, with the frame,
authority, lineage and work-boundary objects, the three accounts of a
construction, and the rule for imports between members (§2); the commitments P0 to P6 with their standing, the
foundation-to-law format with the standing of its consequences, and the
index of material families (§3); the algebra of composition and
conservation, the core result algebra, the conjunction of results and the
demonstration a categorical claim requires (§4); and the hypotheses (§5).

value.label: FOUNDATIONS

value.definition: A foundational claim is a commitment or hypothesis with exactly one standing: recovered, an adopted premise consolidating named source rules without treating them as proof; independent, an adopted premise argued by a case where other commitments hold and it fails; derived, a consequence with named premises; or hypothesis, unestablished by method clause or argument, not law and carried for falsification. This standing differs from result standing and successor disposition.
value.label: Foundational standing

value.definition: Four distinct joins are named: categorical join, a map between categories; composition boundary, a join between successive steps; join of results, closed results combined under one decision rule; and relation join, participant equality in an enclosing relation. An unqualified join in a result context means join of results.

grounding.quote: Four uses of "join" in this corpus are distinct

value.label: Join meanings

value.definition: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, identified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for a subject; representation equality does not establish meaning equality. Interpretation is a declared representation-to-meaning contract in context, naming reliable distinctions and residuals. Context declares subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations under which interpretation holds.

grounding.quote: | Interpretation | a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context; says which distinctions a consumer may rely on and which are residual | P1 |

value.label: Subject, representation, interpretation and context

value.definition: Outcome U is a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval, against which transformation adequacy is judged. Object O is a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding changes.

grounding.quote:
| Outcome U | a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval; adequacy of a transformation is judged against it | P2 |
| Object O | a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), a boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding change | P3 |

value.label: Outcome and object

value.definition: An actor performs a step within a declared envelope of context, attention, time and capability. Roles are occupied relations, not actor kinds; configurations determine which roles exist. A step is bounded work with intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded.

grounding.quote: | Step-produced fact | a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; an observation reproducible from declared sources is re-acquirable and is not one | P0, P4b |

value.label: Actor, step and step-produced fact

value.definition: Claim is an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence is exact admitted observations or artifacts carrying provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability inside a frame creates neither semantic truth nor decision authority. Judgment is a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Authority is identity-bearing permission to operate or dispose acceptance within scope.

grounding.quote: | Judgment | a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation | P6 |

value.label: Claim, evidence, judgment and authority

value.definition: Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or an unproven relation remaining until authorised disposition. Basis is every exact version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter a bound step, claim, result or evaluation. Basis is immutable or moving with declared advancement detection and reevaluation condition; mixed bases require an explicit composite relation. Materiality is evaluation-relative: lawful change can change result, basis validity, admissible evidence, permitted material operator or decision owner; the same criterion applies to uncertainty and closure.

grounding.quote: | Residual | a material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation that remains until an authorised disposition | P4b |

value.label: Residual, basis and materiality

value.definition: Evaluation is a declared question with known admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and, when it performs material action, operation authority. It may seek judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. An evaluation family requires the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording does not establish common family membership.

grounding.quote: | Evaluation family | evaluations that need the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording does not prove that two evaluations share a family | P1, P2 |

value.label: Evaluation and evaluation family

value.definition: Workspace is the bounded material reasoned over or acted upon, potentially including sources, assets, designs, implementation, tools, runtime state, evidence, history, dependencies and human decisions; a repository is only one carrier. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable set of needed variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions; overlapping charts imply neither geometric mathematics nor a runtime abstraction. Coordinate is the complete local basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority position required for interpretation; equality follows a declared relation, not equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology. Topology is the basis-specific structure of material entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle spaces, adjacencies and seams visible to a frame, which need not contain the full workspace topology.

grounding.quote: | Coordinate | the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted: the basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority information the evaluation requires; equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation | P1, P3 |

value.label: Workspace, manifold, coordinate and topology

value.definition: Capability envelope comprises competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation or assurance independence and configuration needed to activate a frame and perform its evaluations. A reference frame is a finite specification of attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for one evaluation family on a basis. An activated frame binds a declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence of correct activation.

grounding.quote: | Activated frame | one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct | P3, P6 |

value.label: Reference frame, activated frame and capability envelope

value.definition: Frame set is a human-declared family available for a governed outcome or workspace. Active frame configuration is the frame activations and declared result relations used for one evaluation or decision. Lens is a reusable question family, becoming a frame only with bounded evaluation, basis, manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and envelope. A role allocates responsibility or authority only through admitted grant; persona changes approach or salience; abstraction hides or contracts detail; component is a structural part. None is a frame by identity alone; components and frames may cross one another.

grounding.quote: | Lens | a reusable family of questions applied across a frame configuration; authority, capability and reuse, temporal behaviour, transport and proof are lenses when named abstractly; a lens becomes a frame only when instantiated with a bounded evaluation, basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and capability envelope | P2 |

value.label: Frame set, configuration, lens and adjacent roles

value.definition: Frame-set authority is human authority declaring or accepting a project frame set; semantic authority owns material-relation meaning; evaluation authority permits evaluation; operation authority is an owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject; decision authority permits accepting, rejecting or otherwise disposing a result. Actor identity is the performing human, agent, tool or process, not authority. Kinds may lawfully coincide but never collapse by default.

grounding.quote:
These may coincide in a lawful case and
never collapse by default.

value.label: Authority kinds

conditions: Governing identity and authority law permits a bounded proxy.
value.definition: Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy. Proxy identity remains distinct from human-authority identity, and the proxy acts only within its existing grant.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may act directly, or through an explicitly
admitted bounded proxy where the governing identity and authority law
permits it; proxy identity and human-authority identity stay distinct

value.label: Bounded proxy

value.definition: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variables, coordinates, evidence or result dependencies for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is procedural separation of activated evaluations from one another's unclosed working results. Assurance independence is claim-relative non-authorship, evidence-acquisition, reference-exposure, actor and configuration separation required by governing assurance law.

grounding.quote: Three relations stay distinct (P6, P1).

value.label: Disjointness and independence

value.definition: The reference-frame tuple is ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩: evaluation family; workspace/topology basis; material manifold; coordinate/equality law; applicable invariants; authority relation; admissible evidence/provenance law; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; closed result algebra or core-mapped refinement; invalidation/rechart condition; actor envelope; and optional declared inter-frame dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs. It specifies an evaluation relation and finite attention scope, not a mandatory schema or runtime carrier.

grounding.quote: A reference frame F is the tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩

value.definition: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:recursive-product-taxonomy, the unchanged concept identities use prefix urn:stdo:concept:recursive-product-taxonomy:. substrate is a lower product/runtime used to build products; development-product is one exact released-product install acting as a source-project builder, adding no product identity or transfer of meaning/authority; source-project is the mutable workspace building the next release cut; release-cut is an immutable annotated release-candidate boundary over a published feature set; product is the released immutable thing resulting from acceptance of that cut; install is a stamped workspace instance of that product; artifact is published output built by a source project or configured installed product; product-definition is the present-tense source-project WHAT authority surface, conventionally PRODUCT.md, not the released artifact.

grounding.quote:

dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

conditions: A product is built with the ODD profile.
value.definition: F18 imports F1 frames/context for acquisition, F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work state/resumption/reuse, F6 claims/evidence/assessment/acceptance, F9 a_c calculus, F10 constitutional chain/outcome/build tenancy, F11 change/ambiguity, F12 project binding, F13 work carriers and F15 release/successor conservation; rules and choices retain owners. Adopted instance premises are I1 selected Product outcome admitted as external authority; I2 mutable workspace beside immutable ledger/event log; I3 bounded probabilistic construction whose reports/artifacts are observations; I4 installed method-product release, possibly an earlier self-release. These premises do not derive from foundations. P0 is recovered, P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent, P4b derived from P0/P2, P5 derived from P0/P6. Table rows distinguish consequences from profile choices and Product/consumer/owner choices; consumer lists add no decision power. §1 restates rules; §16 failure patterns and §19 questions diagnose traced rules; §20 compresses without determinations; §21 records provenance without outcomes.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises hold where a product is built with this profile;
they are adopted with it and do not follow from the foundations (P1, P6):

value.definition: Declared asset graph over state transitions relevant to the product's work; the product's declared program and process space.

The product is expressed as a declared asset graph over the state
transitions relevant to the product's work (P0, P3).

value.label: Declared asset graph

value.definition: Durable truth surface or product asset naming a bounded state of truth. Illustrative product-local nodes are intent, product, requirements, design, module_decomp, code, uat_testcases, integration_tests, bootloader and build targets.

grounding.quote:
Nodes are durable truth surfaces or product assets; each names a bounded
state of truth.

value.label: ODD node

value.definition: Lawful, admissible transition between nodes, declaring required upstream assets, target asset, governing evaluators/gates and output contract.

grounding.quote:
Vectors are the lawful transitions between nodes and are the admissible
transitions of the product.

value.label: ODD vector

value.definition: Named constructive program realising a vector, directly or through a small inner workflow, or serving as a reusable higher-order library function. The outer vector remains its constitutional callable contract.

grounding.quote:
Graph functions are named constructive programs that realise vectors. A
graph function may realise one outer vector directly, refine one outer
vector into a small inner workflow, or act as a reusable higher-order
library function. The outer vector remains the constitutional contract;
the graph function is the constructive realisation of that contract (P4a,
P0).

value.label: Graph function

value.definition: Graph workflow: bind the current target, locate next admissible vectors, traverse one, materialise the next asset, prove the vector closed, and continue until the selected target closes. This description does not instantiate a traversal.

grounding.quote:
The workflow is a traversal over the graph: bind the current target;
locate the next admissible vectors; traverse one vector; materialise the
next asset; prove the vector closed; continue until the selected target
closes.

value.label: ODD traversal

value.definition: ODD work classifications: F_P, urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p, is a bounded probabilistic worker turn under declared policy in one traversal contract; F_D, urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d, is deterministic evaluation/proof over declared traversal properties; F_H, urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h, is explicit human adjudication under declared traversal authority and ambiguity policy. These are ODD concepts, not a_c functor kinds by spelling.

grounding.quote:
Three shorthands name the graph and runtime classifications of work inside
one traversal.

value.label: ODD F_P, F_D and F_H

value.definition: Referenced substrate-neutral source concepts owned by SPEC_METHOD §5: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing and urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication. Only their stated specialisation interfaces are supplied here.

Their full owning clauses are not supplied.

Direction: from the step of

lets a refinement carry an earlier output to a later step only through a

value.definition: Method library has mutable authoring source for future cuts and installed distributions of selected complete immutable cuts. Templates (`*_TEMPLATE.md`) are

value.definition: Structural responsibility layer expressing a capability class bound by the Product to its own domain semantics and published lawful transitions. grounding.quote:
A responsibility layer expresses one capability
class;

value.definition: Audit evaluates a move against the current ODD profile. For the predicate 'the move complies with the current profile', outcomes map compliant→satisfied, non-compliant→falsified, valid and worth incorporating→out_of_frame. Incorporation identifies missing law, this profile as owner and its required update; it is neither compliance nor failure.

grounding.quote:
| compliant | satisfied | the move meets the law of the current profile |
| non-compliant | falsified | the law of this profile that the move violates is the counterexample |
| valid and worth incorporating | out_of_frame | the current profile does not declare the law the move needs; the outcome names that law, this profile as its owner and the update it requires, which is the reconfiguration pressure of out_of_frame ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or indeterminate) |
