value.definition: Authoritative Product WHAT located by product-definition what bindings; default software-development location specification/. Defines intent, product position, goals, requirements and scenarios.
value.label: Product specification WHAT

value.definition: Authoritative Product HOW located by product-definition how bindings; default software-development location build_tenants/. Carries design, GTL publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces.
value.label: Product realisation HOW

value.definition: The role owning traversal, dispatch, actor invocation, process supervision, graph-call realisation, runtime facts, runtime event emission and replay, frames, continuations, retry and correction control, closure folds over runtime truth, re-entry after publish boundaries, lineage and provenance.
value.label: ABG

value.definition: The domain product owning domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections, and domain closure and gap interpretation.

grounding.quote:
The ODD product owns domain asset meaning, graph-function meaning, the
published function catalogue, policy overlays, domain query projections,
and closure and gap interpretation for its domain (P6, P1).

value.label: ODD product

value.definition: Service and query surfaces, including downstream read models, transport, sessions, routing, browser-safe projections and APIs. Their exposure of information supplies neither runtime nor continuation ownership.

grounding.quote:
Service or query layers may own transport, sessions, routing,
browser-safe projection and API surfaces. They own neither runtime truth
nor continuation truth. The real constructive carrier is never hidden
behind the word service (P6).

value.label: Service and query layers

value.definition: Explicit typed assets or nodes with typed domain boundaries; an asset that is a real produced or consumed boundary has a declared asset_surface.

grounding.quote:
Concrete assets must bind explicitly into
typed domain boundaries. Where an asset is a real produced or consumed boundary,
its `asset_surface` is declared (P3).

value.label: Typed domain assets and nodes

value.definition: A named GraphFunction or lawful composition is the operative constructive carrier. Its public outer callable contract remains distinct from inner executable vectors.

grounding.quote:
Every operative constructive step is carried by one named `GraphFunction`
or one lawful graph-function composition.

value.label: GraphFunction

value.definition: An outcome traversal declares governed movement before implementation: source and target asset types, edge traversal or graph-function name, closure or evaluation obligation, lineage obligation, ambiguity or gap obligation, and allowed F_D, F_P and F_H bindings. Its declarative carrier comprises GTL graph functions, typed nodes, vectors, operator and evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy, projection and lineage ledger declarations.

grounding.quote:
An outcome traversal declares the governed movement before
implementation: source asset type; target asset type; edge traversal or
graph-function name; closure or evaluation obligation; lineage obligation;
ambiguity or gap obligation; allowed `F_D`, `F_P` and `F_H` bindings. The
declarative carrier structure is GTL graph functions, typed nodes,
vectors, operator bindings, evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy
declarations, projection declarations and lineage ledger declarations
(P0, P3).

value.label: Outcome traversal

value.definition: The GTL module is the operative publication surface for public graph-function carriers, traversed graphs, typed nodes and vectors, outer callable contracts and published refinement boundaries. The live function catalogue is machine-readable; the loop's ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes for ABG consumption.

grounding.quote:
The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue. At
minimum each retained function should expose its name, inputs, outputs,
intent, and public or helper role.

The product must publish the public graph-function carriers, the graph or
graphs those carriers traverse, typed node and vector surfaces, and the
semantic jobs or equivalent outer callable contracts bound to the public
carrier.
| `ActionCatalog` | Published lawful graph actions: graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs, and eligible outcomes. | GTL/product publication consumed by ABG. |

value.label: GTL module and function catalogues

value.definition: The constructive evaluation or homeostasis loop runs from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to the next lawful action. Its four distinct functions are synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action. It corrects toward required conditions as observations arrive, without guaranteeing convergence or adequacy of those conditions.

grounding.quote:
Every ODD product over GTL/ABG must preserve one constructive evaluation
loop running from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation
to the next lawful action. This is the profile's homeostasis loop, and
its constitutional surface names the operative functions directly:
`synthesize_model`, `eval_gap`, `evaluate_next` and `evaluate_action`
(P2, P5, P6). The loop is this profile's binding of
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation):
it corrects towards the required conditions as observations arrive,
guarantees neither convergence nor the adequacy of those conditions, and
its diagnoses distinguish the four causes named there (P2, P6).

value.label: Constructive evaluation loop

value.definition: IntentLineage is admitted source intent and lineage references from human, imported source, prior product, intent engine or prior synthesized construction intent, grounded in ABG event-log truth and unable to invent graph actions. ProductAssetModel is desired and known typed asset truth synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth; its publication basis uses admitted events and product projection references, not runtime or action authority. Worksite is workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and observed file/process state, an observable substrate without authority by itself. RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted runtime facts owned by ABG. RuntimeProjection is ABG replay-derived state over log and execution basis. ObservationSnapshot is a read-only runtime/worksite view, an ABG evaluator carrier with product domain rows. GapPressureRow is product meaning over admitted observation, describing missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous assets and evidence.

grounding.quote:
| `ObservationSnapshot` | Read-only view of runtime truth plus worksite facts relevant to construction. | ABG evaluator carrier with product domain rows. |
| `GapPressureRow` | Typed pressure over missing, partial, blocked, waiting, or ambiguous assets and evidence. | Product domain meaning over admitted observation. |

| `RuntimeEventLog` | Append-only admitted runtime facts. | ABG runtime truth. |
| `RuntimeProjection` | Replay-derived current runtime state over event log and execution basis. | ABG projection truth. |

value.label: Intent, model, worksite and observation carriers

value.definition: TargetObligationBinding binds gap pressure exactly to the externally selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence references and admissible graph outcomes; it is product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible policy through ABG evaluator kernel and product policy. ConstructionIntent is the admitted selected action for one bounded graph invocation preserving the target binding's outcome and bounded-basis references, under ABG admission and traversal authority.

grounding.quote: | `TargetObligationBinding` | Exact binding from gap pressure to the selected Product outcome, any admitted prerequisite or experiment basis, target assets, required roles, evidence refs, and admissible graph outcomes. | Product domain binding over GTL/ABG action authority. |

| `PriorityProjection` | Deterministic ranking over bound lawful actions under visible policy. | ABG evaluator kernel plus product policy. |
| `ConstructionIntent` | Admitted selected action for one bounded graph invocation, preserving the selected outcome or admitted bounded-basis refs carried by its target binding. | ABG admission and traversal authority. |

value.label: Target binding, priority and construction intent

value.definition: AdmittedEvidence comprises admitted worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence, under ABG/product admission rather than worker self-closure. EdgeFulfillmentLedger is closure evidence and convergence truth for one edge attempt/version, including counts, obligation rows, materialization, liveness and admission references and edge_converged. EdgeClosureDecision is the closed sum type close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice or block. NextActionBasis distinguishes initial_selection, post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice and post_block; it supplies dispatch basis, not another controller. NextActionProjection observes this basis and current truth and selects a next graph action only when lawful, under ABG evaluation and product policy.

grounding.quote:
| `AdmittedEvidence` | Admitted worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness, and postflight evidence. | ABG/product admission, not worker self-closure. |
| `EdgeFulfillmentLedger` | Evidence and convergence carrier for one edge attempt or version. | Closure evidence truth. |
| `EdgeClosureDecision` | Sum type over the ledger: close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice, block. | Closure decision truth. |
| `NextActionProjection` | Read model that observes `NextActionBasis` plus current truth and selects a next graph action only when lawful. | ABG next-action evaluation projection with product policy. |

| `NextActionBasis` | Sum type naming why `evaluate_next` is being called: `initial_selection`, `post_yield_resume`, `post_close_graph_continuation`, `post_retry`, `post_repair`, `post_reenter`, `post_reprice`, or `post_block`. `post_reprice` records a re-entry request and carries no action-selection authority. | Dispatch basis for next-action evaluation. It is not a separate controller. |

value.label: Evidence, ledger, closure and next-action carriers

value.definition: synthesize_model takes IntentLineage, prior ProductAssetModel and admitted product truth to produce ProductAssetModel. eval_gap takes ProductAssetModel, RuntimeEventLog, RuntimeProjection and Worksite to produce ObservationSnapshot and GapPressureRow. evaluate_next takes NextActionBasis, fresh eval_gap, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog and Policy to produce PriorityProjection, NextActionProjection and selected_action, plus a distinct core result when returning typed no-action. evaluate_action takes ConstructionIntent, AdmittedEvidence, TargetObligationBinding and Policy to produce EdgeFulfillmentLedger and EdgeClosureDecision. These are four authority functions even if libraries are shared.

grounding.quote:
The loop has one model-synthesis function and three distinct evaluation
functions. They may share underlying libraries; they must not share
authority (P6):

| `evaluate_action` | `ConstructionIntent + AdmittedEvidence + TargetObligationBinding + Policy` | `EdgeFulfillmentLedger + EdgeClosureDecision` | Action-result evaluation. It decides close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice, or block for the action just taken. It does not choose the next graph action. |

value.label: Model synthesis and three evaluation functions

value.definition: Source-defined result domains distinguish edge-obligation evaluation, candidate availability, next-action selectability and candidate acceptance. Closure decisions and their cause refinements map to exactly one core value without adding a core value; their domain vocabulary and basis/reason references remain alongside that value. Invocational selection and ordinary empty selection after graph completion are not themselves core results. ACTIVATION dispositions accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject concern candidate acceptance and are not closure decisions.

grounding.quote:
The closure decision is `evaluate_action`'s result over admitted
evidence, mapped for the predicate "the edge's obligations are fulfilled
on the exact basis". The bounded action it judges has its own step result
under [ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)
for "a candidate is available", and neither value counts toward the
other's predicate
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).

value.label: Distinct loop result predicates

value.definition: Agentic conformance has an F_P walkthrough proving the constitutional process can be followed and an F_D deterministic artifact-admission gate. The agentic coder reasons, drafts and proposes from a minimal declared authority packet. The walkthrough covers real intake triage, smallest lawful re-entry, specification, requirement, design and ticket chain, constructive evaluation and closure proof.

grounding.quote:
Conformance has two halves: an F_P proof that the process can be followed,
and an F_D gate that admits the produced artifacts (P6).

value.label: Agentic conformance

value.definition: Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces that connect feature/use-case intent, initial assets, vectors, significant paths and closing evidence. Real authority-path negative proof is closure-grade evidence obtained by invalidating a real authority-bearing input and exercising the supported Product path, rather than fabricating the expected refusal.

grounding.quote:
Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces, not only test
documentation. A scenario bundle should make clear which feature or
use-case boundary is exercised; which assets are expected to exist before
the scenario starts; which vectors are expected to be traversed; which
significant paths are expected to be exercised; and what evidence closes
the scenario (P2, P6).

Negative proof for an ODD or graph-native boundary exercises the supported
Product authority path. It must not manufacture the refusal state, blocked
event, gap or verdict that the system is supposed to derive (P6, P5;
provenance rc.2 #117b-real-authority-path-negative-proof-stdo-up-010).

value.label: Scenario and authority-path proving surfaces

value.definition: ODD cold-start routes are ordered acquisition procedures for a concrete product. The profile supplies structural expectations, the product-specific method supplies domain law, and local product surfaces supply the current build line.

grounding.quote: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product, read in the order below (P1, P2).

It is a derived acquisition surface of same-digest sections §1, §2, §11.1–§11.5D, §11.7 and §11.7A and owns no determination.

value.definition: The ODD successor provenance register reports receipt of all 48 rc.2 ODD_METHOD rows under STDO-UP-015, with conserved modal force, exact formal tables/code and rewritten prose. It records successor member names, imperative-to-indicative restatement preserving force, labelled axiom paragraphs and British prose spelling with identifiers unchanged. Rows of rc.2 ODD_METHOD.md received by this member, all 48 under
STDO-UP-015. Anchors are into rc.2 ODD_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of
this file. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own text at

value.definition: POSTING_GUIDE owns the commentary layer: purpose, authority boundary, locations, identity, categories, structure, discussion state, posting rules and ratification. It consumes PRODUCT_DEFINITION's comment binding, TICKETS' work carriers, SPEC_METHOD's authority surfaces and EVALUATION's claims/evidence without defining them. Shared-method adoption is owned by SPEC_METHOD §6. Principle references P0–P6 and rc.2 routes identify stated grounds and provenance; the predecessor cut is not an application dependency.

Guide. Owns the commentary layer of a governed project: what a post is
for, its boundary with authority, where posts live, their identity,
categories and structure, their discussion state, the posting rules and
ratification. Consumes
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)

(the surfaces that carry authority) and [EVALUATION §1](EVALUATION.md#1-claims)
(claims and evidence); defines none of them.

value.label: Posting guide

value.definition: A post is working commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff and repricing confidence. It is not constitutional truth, though it may later influence specification or design.

grounding.quote:
A post is not constitutional truth. It is working commentary, and it may
later influence specification or design (P6).

value.label: Post

Default filenames use YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS_CATEGORY_SUBJECT.md, with 20260327T120000_REVIEW_bootloader-boundary.md as an example. Alternative carriers retain stable identity, publication time, category, subject, author, discussion state and supersession history.

Posts live at the location the product definition binds as
`ticketing.comments.root` (P6, P3; rc.2 #location). The default local-file
binding is:

```text
.ai-workspace/comments/<agent>/

The subject should be short, specific and stable enough to scan later
(P3). A carrier that is not a file must preserve an equivalent stable post
identity, publication time, category, subject, author, discussion state
and supersession history (P3, P4b).

value.definition: A post takes one of six categories: REVIEW critiques code, specification, design or another post; STRATEGY proposes technical or methodological direction; GAP identifies precise insufficiency or contradiction; SCHEMA describes data/event model, interface or contract shape; HANDOFF transfers bounded context or task state; MATRIX compares decision options explicitly.
value.label: Post categories

MATRIX uses a decision table for its central section. Discussion Status distinguishes Draft (author still shaping), Open (published active discussion) and Closed (discussion concluded).

value.definition: The POSTING_GUIDE provenance register reports conservation of predecessor boundary, location, identity, categories, structure, mutability, posting rules and ratification rows at §§2–9, with shared-method adoption restated in SPEC_METHOD §6 and referenced at §10. Imperative category/template headings retain requirement force in indicative form; predecessor title prose is restated in §1; Product authorization becomes Product authorisation. These are provenance assertions, not independent proof of conservation.

Rows of rc.2 POSTING_GUIDE.md. Anchors are into rc.2 POSTING_GUIDE.md; a
locus is a section of this file unless another member is named. Every
conserved row is restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is

value.definition: PRODUCT_DEFINITION is a tier-2 member owning project binding: overlays and layout independence, required relations, constitutional-set sufficiency, installed basis and manager, semantic resolution, local constitution, collective reference frames, WHAT/HOW/work carriers, discovery/composition, conformance, one constitutional surface/version boundary and bootstrap. It owns product-definition-routing (§§1–4,9,12), semantic-resolution (§§5,6,10) and build-tenancy (§8). It consumes tier-1 concepts without redefining them; SPEC_METHOD owns generic WHAT/HOW and build-tenant law, FOUNDATIONS Product lineage, RELEASE release identities/cohorts/selectors and ASSURANCE assurance/testing. Its schemas, templates, filenames, fields and commands are Product realisation interoperability shapes, not profile terms.

grounding.quote:
The schemas, templates, filenames, manifest
fields and commands named here are this Product's own realisation shapes,
accepted as interoperability boundaries under §11; they are not profile
terms. Three bounded contexts the predecessor placed in its SPEC_METHOD are
owned here: product-definition-routing (§1 to §4, §9, §12),
semantic-resolution (§5, §6, §10) and build-tenancy (§8).

value.label: PRODUCT_DEFINITION member

value.definition: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing under the selected complete STDO basis, the definition overlay locates governing surfaces and records relations without owning their content. One JSON definition represents each distinct current product WHAT. stdo_<label>.json is conventional; stdo_default.json is the default for a source project with one definition. schemas/product-definition.schema.json is the normative interoperability schema and templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json the single fill-in form; neither is another semantic owner. The definition root is its containing directory.

grounding.quote:
Every product defined under this method publishes one JSON definition for
each distinct current product WHAT. Its conventional filename is
`stdo_<label>.json`; `stdo_default.json` is the default for a source
project with one product definition. A directory may hold more than one
definition when it hosts more than one distinct product WHAT, and only
then. Several build tenants realising the same WHAT are entries in one definition and
never add definition files (P3).

value.label: Product definition overlay

value.definition: Definition Label is a stable lowercase discovery label using ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique only within its directory and not Product identity. product.definition_id is a URI identifying a continuing mutable WHAT-definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition set, distinct from immutable Product and release identities. Definition, Product, bounded-context and build-tenant URIs are identity carriers subject to owning authority and IDENTITY law, not self-authorising strings.

grounding.quote:
The suffix `<label>` is the Definition Label: a stable lowercase local
discovery label of ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique
only among the definitions in the same directory. It is not Product
identity. The `product.definition_id` URI inside the definition is the
Product-Definition Identity: the stable identity of the mutable
product-definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition
set. It identifies one continuing WHAT definition, not one immutable
released Product (P3).

value.definition: F12 traces project-binding consequences from commitments and instance premises: own authorities, chosen layout, shared workspace, recurring terms and released method. It records P0 as recovered, P1/P2/P3/P6 as independent, P5 as derived from P0/P6 with the open-world premise, and P4b as derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts where those commitments occur. Its ten rows cover overlay, identity/discovery/composition, constitutional sufficiency, installed release/adoption, context resolution, imports, collective frame basis, WHAT/HOW/work carriers, one constitutional surface/version boundary and bootstrap. Added domain/interoperability choices remain with the owners named in each row; imports remain owned by FOUNDATIONS §2.

grounding.quote:
This family (F12 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides how one project binds to the method. Its instance premises, which
the commitments do not supply, are named in the rows as follows: own
authorities, a project has its own product WHAT under its own authorities
and adopts the method without becoming part of it; chosen layout, the
project's governing documents, realisations and work carriers already
live where the project placed them; shared workspace, several projects,
product definitions, tenants and actors share one workspace or machine;
recurring terms, one term occurs in several bounded contexts with
different meanings; released method, the method is published as
immutable released versions that a project selects, installs and later
replaces. The index also assigns to this family the rule of
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members);
the table traces that rule in its sixth row, whose rule column names that
section, and owns none of it. Each commitment's standing is written as the
table of commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

value.label: Foundation family F12

value.definition: A Constitutional Set is the complete selected set of governing documents for a product, irrespective of file count. It collectively makes recoverable axioms (starting truths, invariants, refusal conditions), ontology (kinds, identities, relations, boundaries, lifecycle), epistemology (evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification and decision authority), taxonomy (classifications and kind distinctions), and semantics (meaning of terms, relations, states, operations and outcomes).

grounding.quote:
A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected
for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected
set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1; rc.2
#constitutional-set-sufficiency):

- axioms: irreducible starting truths, invariants and refusal conditions;
- ontology: the kinds of things treated as real and their material
  identities, relations, boundaries and lifecycle;
- epistemology: how claims become knowable or acceptable, including
  admissible evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification and
  decision authority;
- taxonomy: the classifications and kind distinctions that prevent
  category collapse; and
- semantics: the governed meaning of terms, relations, states, operations
  and outcomes.

value.label: Constitutional Set

value.definition: Installed Release Basis is the pair of an immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI and installed-manifest SHA-256. The manifest supplies transport/integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution.

value.definition: An Adoption Plan is a read-only deterministic acceptance object binding current Product Definition identity and bytes, current basis, and a resolved immutable target cut, annotated tag object, commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. grounding.quote:
An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
under the same law.

value.definition: Semantic Import applies the FOUNDATIONS import definition to a declared target scope, preserving unchanged meaning, direction, loss and lack of authority. Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import. Semantic Equivalence requires governing authorities to establish equality while each concept retains its owner and context; neither spelling nor opposing translations proves it. Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating competitors; a selected foreign concept enters only through a declared import, translation or equivalence.

grounding.quote: | Semantic Disambiguation | not an import: it selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. Where the selected concept is owned in another bounded context, it enters that scope only by the import, translation or equivalence its carrier declares (§6) |

| Semantic Equivalence | not an import: each concept keeps its own owner and context, and neither adopts the other's meaning. It requires the governing authorities to establish the claimed equality; neither identical spelling nor two opposing translations proves it automatically |

The frame objects, the step that activates a frame,
the core result algebra with its conjunction, and qualification belong to
other members; this member imports them unchanged and defines none of them

value.label: Reference-frame member

conditions: Applies wherever the governing Product or method permits the relevant human, agentic, deterministic, probabilistic, assurance or mixed work.

An activated frame combines evaluation family, exact workspace/topology basis, finite material relations/coordinates, invariants/authorities, admissible evidence/exclusions and capability envelope, yielding one closed core result. The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit: the unit that is
activated and evaluated as one bounded context.

This member owns the reference-frame-evaluation
bounded context, `urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation`,
under its exact publication basis.

value.label: Reference frame and engagement context

Their source contexts are their members because those members declare no bounded-context identity.

FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and
EVALUATION declare no bounded-context identity, so each row's source
context is its member (P1, P3).
| the frame tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩ | FOUNDATIONS | [The frame tuple](FOUNDATIONS.md#the-frame-tuple), FOUNDATIONS §2 |

value.label: Reference-frame declared import population

value.definition: The frames-and-context family F1 concerns finite actors declaring, sizing, binding, activating, relating, auditing and revising bounded reference frames. REFERENCE_FRAME owns engagement law in urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation; ACTIVATION owns context construction and FOUNDATIONS owns the referenced frame objects, authority kinds, independence distinctions and frame tuple. The foundation-to-law table traces rules and choices without owning those rules.

grounding.quote:
This family, frames and context (F1 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law)),
decides how a finite actor engages a body of work through bounded reference
frames: how a frame is declared, sized, bound, activated, related to other
frames, used to audit coverage and revised.

value.label: Frames and context

value.definition: A reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required by one evaluation family. It is a relation specification, not a required schema or runtime carrier. Its engagement atomicity means activation and evaluation as one bounded attention unit; it does not imply semantic irreducibility.

grounding.quote: a reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations one evaluation family requires.

A reference frame is atomic at engagement altitude: it is activated and
evaluated as one bounded attention unit. Semantic irreducibility is a
separate question: one frame may contain several semantic atoms, and one
semantic atom may take part in several frames

value.label: Reference frame

value.definition: The questions or predicates a frame declares it supports at its declared coordinates, together with its closed result algebra. This declaration supplies the boundary against which sufficiency can be tested.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

value.label: Evaluation family

value.definition: A selected actor's declared limits and capabilities, including competence, context capacity, access and tools. An activated attention surface must fit this envelope; adequate attention in actual use is a separate evidential question.

grounding.quote:
Whether the actor attends adequately to a frame that fits is a separate
question, answered by actual-use evidence under
[EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification); a size measurement
does not answer it

value.label: Capability envelope

value.definition: Authority admitted from its existing owner and scope. Frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority remain distinguishable, with actor identity apart; frame-set authority is human authority. An authority proxy remains distinct from the human authority.

grounding.quote: the division into frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority, with actor identity apart, and frame-set authority as human authority: FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds

value.label: Admitted authority

value.definition: A semantic atom is a domain meaning unit whose irreducibility is distinct from engagement atomicity. A domain's semantic-contraction law, where supplied by an adopting method, governs that domain atom family.

grounding.quote:
Where an adopting
method supplies a semantic-contraction law for its domain atoms, that law
governs the domain atom family.

value.label: Semantic atom

value.definition: Human-declared project method structure comprising selected frames, evaluation inventory, capability envelopes, overlaps, checks, dependencies, authorities, exclusions, residual uncertainty and revision conditions for a governed workspace and outcome. It need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated
development practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the governed
outcome's risk and knowledge of the available agents and other actors.
a frame set need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology

value.label: Frame set

conditions: An evaluation was performed.
value.definition: One closed result in the declared core algebra or a lawful refinement mapped into it. The five named core values are satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis; FOUNDATIONS §4 owns their meanings. A nonperformed evaluation has no evaluation result.

grounding.quote:
Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
(`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
`invalid_basis`)

value.label: Closed evaluation result

value.definition: Seven relations distinct from the frame: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame or activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result plus evidence plus residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision, conflict or indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value, declared_loss or refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. These signatures describe relations rather than callable software interfaces; subsequent text supplements the signatures' outcome lists.

grounding.quote:
declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities)
  -> frame_set

activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor)
  -> activated_frame | activation_refusal

evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence)
  -> result + evidence + residuals

conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results)
  -> decision | conflict | indeterminate

translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping)
  -> translated_value | declared_loss | refusal

audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set)
  -> coverage_ledger

revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change)
  -> proposed_frame_set_delta

value.label: Method functions

value.definition: A declared decision rule consumes closed results of several frames using the conjunction and core values owned by FOUNDATIONS §4. REFERENCE_FRAME defines the frame relation and outcome refinement, not another conjunction.

grounding.quote:
A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
this member defines no conjunction of its own.

value.label: Result conjunction

value.definition: One frame supplies a value or evidence consumed inside another through a declared translation. Its fields are source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

grounding.quote:
One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions

value.label: Evidence or coordinate translation

conditions: The evaluation requires composition.
value.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application.

grounding.quote:
Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition

value.label: Material composition

value.definition: Named frame relation categories: disjoint shares no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations; overlapping shares some material variables, evidence or entities; complementary evaluations jointly inform one decision; alternative frames evaluate the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves another frame's aggregated material distinction; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another's domain; translated moves values or evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporally successive evaluates a changed basis later; composed combines frame relations into one governed evaluation or action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where real authority or decomposition exists.

grounding.quote:
- governing and subordinate: one frame inherits declared constraints from
  another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.

value.label: Frame relation categories

value.definition: Exchange of information between frames or their activated actors. Communication is distinct from functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency.

grounding.quote:
Communication is the exchange of
information between frames, or between the actors activated on them. An
exchange by itself grants no authority

value.label: Communication

value.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T) binds workspace, governed outcome, exact basis, known evaluation inventory, declared frame set, and claim time or immutable checkpoint.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
checkpoint T of the claim.

value.label: Coverage basis

value.definition: The known material evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, with provenance and materiality recorded.

grounding.quote:
The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every
material available source

value.label: Evaluation inventory

value.definition: Cross-cutting audit lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/interaction seams, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression, and actor capability/context fit. A lens becomes a frame only when separately instantiated as a bounded evaluation family.

grounding.quote:
These are lenses (FOUNDATIONS §2): they become frames only when separately
instantiated as bounded evaluation families

value.label: Coverage dimensions

value.definition: Per-evaluation audit record whose status answers whether, on the declared coverage tuple, a capable selected frame covers the evaluation without unresolved frame/result/authority conflict, or a cited governing authority excludes it. Baseline statuses are covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown and excluded_by_authority.

grounding.quote:
They answer
whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate "on the
declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with
no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that
cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it".

value.label: Coverage ledger

value.definition: Ordered examination of activation, exact subject/basis, actor capability, admissible evidence, missing material variables/invariants, missing conjunction/translation, evaluation-family adequacy and only then the need for another frame.

grounding.quote:
1. Was the correct declared frame activated?
2. Were the subject and basis exact?
3. Was the actor inside the capability envelope?
4. Was admissible evidence available?
5. Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame?
6. Is a required conjunction or translation missing?
7. Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete?
8. Is another frame required?

value.label: Frame diagnosis

value.definition: Carrier-neutral packet for one activated frame or declared active frame configuration. The minimal binding template identifies the activation and resolves the frame, exact evaluation, subject, basis, attention, actor, authorities, evidence, inter-frame relations, result return and stop/change conditions.

grounding.quote:
An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
workspace from ambient context

The following carrier-neutral content is sufficient to bind one declared
frame for one evaluation.

value.label: Activation packet and binding template

value.definition: Three carrier-neutral document shapes supplying the least content to declare a frame, frame set and evaluation result. They are source templates, not populated declarations or executed evaluations.

grounding.quote:
The three carrier-neutral shapes below are the least content that declares
a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result. Each is sufficient as
written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier

value.label: Minimal declaration templates

value.definition: A historical mapping from received rc.2 REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD anchors to dispositions and successor loci; unqualified loci refer to REFERENCE_FRAME. Rows received by FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION or EVALUATION are listed there. This section records dispositions rather than deciding substantive law.

RF rows received by this member. Rows that land in FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION
or EVALUATION are listed in those members. Anchors are into rc.2
REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless it names

value.definition: Tier-2 RELEASE owns release publication: bounded context, release identities, project-qualified references/subtrees, historical reference conservation, candidate construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification, monotonic version-line advancement, selectors, naming, scoped assets, Product subject, release-matched asset cohorts, acceptance, external qualification dependencies and successor baseline conservation STDO-UP-015 with its dispositions. Its context identity is urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication under the selected complete STDO basis. It owns qualification/publication/selection transitions, not Product meaning or consumer adoption.

Tier 2. Owns release publication: the release-publication bounded
context, release identities, project-qualified refs and the project
subtree, historical ref conservation, the three phases with candidate
construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification and
monotonic version-line advancement

STDO basis. It owns the identities and transitions used to qualify,

consumer adoption

value.label: Release publication

value.definition: A published immutable point-in-time RC cut with product-local name v<version>-rc.<n>. Release process evaluates, bounds, names, publishes and makes the cut discoverable, distinct from live specification's current constitutional project truth.

grounding.quote:
Release process is distinct from live project specification. Live
specification defines the current constitutional truth of the project.
Release process defines how one published point-in-time cut is evaluated,
bounded, named, published and made discoverable

value.label: Release cut

value.definition: The mutable product-local v<version> selector points to the latest published immutable RC for its project and version line, where latest is the greatest published positive RC ordinal. It is a discovery aid.

It denotes a mutable version-line selector (FOUNDATIONS §2). The selector
points to the latest published immutable RC cut on that line, where latest
means the greatest positive RC ordinal published for that project and
version line.

value.label: Version-line selector

value.definition: F15 is the release and successor-conservation family. Its instance premises are recursive products, published point-in-time cuts for uncontrolled consumers, mutable and possibly shared carriers, source-matched derived assets, external service dependencies, and predecessor/successor lines. These premises are not supplied by the commitments. The table traces but does not own FOUNDATIONS §2 lineage objects. Cited standing is P0 recovered; P1, P3 and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; P5 derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are
named in the rows as follows:

value.label: Release foundation-to-law map

value.definition: The lineage roles are substrate, development product, source project, release cut, Product, install, artifact and product definition. Each binds its own identity and basis. A mutable source workspace has no fixed Product identity. An install used as builder substrate is bound as a development product. A product definition is a source-project surface, distinct from a released artifact.

value.label: Project Release Namespace

grounding.quote:
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;

value.label: Project Subtree

The optional Release Branch is a mutable convenience carrier aligned to the selector's latest-published commit.

- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

value.definition: An Immutable RC Cut is an annotated project-qualified Git tag together with its exact Product release subject. It names one published candidate and, once accepted, one released Product; it realises the generic release cut.
value.label: Immutable RC Cut

value.definition: The Version-Line Selector is a mutable project-qualified tag alias naming the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for one project and version line. It is discovery, not an exact operative basis or consumer-selection authority.
value.label: Version-Line Selector

value.definition: The release process has ordered phases: mutable candidate construction; immutable RC publication with monotonic version-line advancement; exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption. Publication provides one exact subject for review, replay and possible acceptance.
value.label: Release process

value.definition: Exact-cut qualification evaluates claims on their bound immutable subject and evidence. Acceptance is the human Product authority's verdict on that exact subject, distinct from publication, selector advancement, operation outcomes and consumer adoption.

grounding.quote:
An RC is accepted only when the required exact-cut review and operator
checks are complete and the human authority accepts that exact subject.

value.label: Exact-cut qualification and acceptance

value.definition: Consumer adoption is a separate explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs, verifies and pins an immutable RC. Its read-only Adoption Plan binds current definition bytes and basis to the target cut, annotated tag object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, producing a deterministic plan digest. Fleet adoption uses one aggregate digest over all exact per-definition plans.

grounding.quote:
Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable RC.

The read-only plan,
the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest.

value.label: Consumer adoption and Adoption Plan

value.definition: Optional release-scoped surfaces include release notes, release and installed-distribution manifests, dependency declarations, package or installed-carrier metadata, qualification receipts, and branch/tag identity declarations.
value.label: Release-scoped assets

value.definition: The Product release subject is the declared exact member set or artifact, distinguished from its release-scoped claims and excluded co-located mutable source fields. A repository commit is the wider carrier; its subtree tree and member inventory identify the subject within it.

grounding.quote:
A repository commit carries those declared sets but does not make every
co-located file or sibling Project Subtree a Product member. The exact
Project Subtree tree and Product member inventory distinguish the subject
from the wider carrier.

value.label: Product subject and repository carrier

conditions: A Product authority explicitly declares the relation when a source corpus and required distributed or derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set.
value.definition: A Release-Matched Asset Cohort names every required Product and asset, exact source dependency, owning authorities, qualification boundary and publication transaction. The closed release-matched STDO stack contains the exact standards corpus cut; its distributed spec plugin and host assets; exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product used for validation/projection; exact STDO Representation Product; and its released a_c.STDO program and logical constraint map or equivalent semantic index, including complete source inventory, member digests, member-set digest and derivation cut identity.

grounding.quote:
The declaring
relation names every required Product and asset, the exact source
dependency, its owning authorities, the qualification boundary and the
publication transaction.

value.label: Release-Matched Asset Cohort

conditions: A coordinated STDO cohort is being constructed.
value.definition: Two-commit construction avoids self-reference because installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object. Commit A freezes STDO source and qualification material; its local unpushed tag is installed and verified to obtain the manifest identity. Commit B freezes derived Products, index and cohort record. One qualified atomic transaction publishes the carrier branch and complete Product ref set.

grounding.quote:
Exact installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object,
so a same-commit carrier containing both that identity and derived child
bytes would be self-referential.

value.label: Two-commit cohort publication

value.definition: An external qualification dependency is a backend, transport or operator-facing service outside the local carrier. It can remain outside Product for carrier/migration classification while blocking a dependent claim. A clean skip is an evaluation not performed, with no result.

grounding.quote:
Such a dependency may remain out of
Product for carrier and migration classification while still blocking the
dependent release claim

value.label: External qualification dependency

value.definition: A successor disposition is a claim about one predecessor claim: conserved means retained; superseded means replaced by an accepted successor relation; intentionally removed means removed by current Product authority; not applicable means no successor effect with a bounded reason. These predicates are not result values or the acceptance disposition of an assessed candidate. Evaluation records its own core result with the predicate; an unresolved disposition states no claim, has no result and is a planned assessment without a closed result.

grounding.quote:
An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result: in the
qualification of the affected claim it is a planned assessment without a
closed result, which is why it blocks that qualification

value.label: Semantic successor disposition

value.definition: The source-disposition register records claimed conservation and loci for received rc.2 RELEASE_METHOD.md rows. Routes are provenance only. Its editorial generalisations remove identity emphasis, replace local references with §9 or 'this member', use British spelling, and express 'need to remain usable' as a declaration condition rather than a new obligation. Generic release objects are defined in FOUNDATIONS and realised here. The register reports new Results, foundation-map and disposition-evaluation material without itself deciding conservation.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

value.label: Release source-disposition register

value.definition: SPEC_METHOD is the Tier 2 particular method and process constitution. It owns method identity, constitutional chain and surfaces, manifesto and litmus tests, requirement/design and trace law, live-surface and outcome conservation, triage/classification, consistency and sprint boundaries, ambiguity and lifecycle sufficiency, lineage/version boundary, migration, procedures, design-record conventions and build-tenant binding. It is realised from FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION, not foundational; its mechanisms could differ under the same principles. PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns project binding, ASSURANCE testing law, TICKETS work carriers and RELEASE release mechanics.

grounding.quote:
nothing here is foundational, every clause
names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3), and each
mechanism could be realised differently under the same principles.

value.label: SPEC_METHOD process constitution

value.definition: Spec-driven development treats specification as constitutional source to make software re-derivable, auditable and correctable under explicit authority. Its declarative preference is to declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence surfaces, with lawful processing realising work. It is a meta-constitution for relations among goals, intent, product, requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing, sufficiency and authority during iteration.

grounding.quote:
Its
overriding bias is declarative rather than imperative: the system should
primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence
surfaces, and let lawful processing derive and realise work from that
declared surface.

Its role is meta-constitutional: it defines how goals, intent, product,
requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing relate; what counts as
specification sufficiency; what kinds of requirement truth exist; and how
authority flows during iterative delivery.

value.label: Spec-driven development

conditions: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:method-identity under the selected complete basis.
value.definition: STDO abbreviates four named areas of method law: S Specification owned by SPEC_METHOD; T Ticketing owned by TICKETS; D Design owned by DESIGN_MODULE; O Outcome-Driven Development, whose complete area identity and realisation meaning are owned by ODD.

grounding.quote:
S,
Specification, owned by this member; T, Ticketing, owned by
[TICKETS](TICKETS.md); D, Design, owned by the design profile member
[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md); and O, Outcome-Driven Development, the
complete area whose identity and realisation meaning are owned by its
profile member [ODD](ODD.md).

value.label: STDO method identity

value.definition: F10 explains how specification governs realisations, conditional on owned layers, layered interpretable surfaces, potentially several changing realisations and immutable releases. It distinguishes consequences from added choices and their owners. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Standing of the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0
recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and
P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5
derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise.

value.label: Chain, outcome and build-tenant foundation map

value.definition: Goals define current overriding concerns for a bounded work wave. They keep temporary focus out of deeper layers until intentional repricing, are more immediate than intent, and higher-level than product definition and requirements.

grounding.quote:
The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it captures the current
overriding concerns for the next body of work, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements.

value.label: Goals

value.definition: Intent states purpose, direction and directional scope. It carries optional realisation detail only when that detail is constitutional.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope; it carries
no optional realisation detail unless that detail is itself constitutional.

value.label: Intent

value.definition: The product-definition surface states the current mutable source project's realisation, terms, boundaries and end-state shape in present-tense, requirement-decomposable form. It bridges direction to obligation and routes actual authority locations; it is neither released cut nor installed Product, release note nor rival truth surface.

grounding.quote:
The product-definition surface is the bridge
between direction and obligation: it states the current product definition
of the mutable source project in present-tense terms, names the product
terms and boundaries that downstream layers rely on, and provides the
surface that requirements decompose. It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product;

value.label: Product Definition surface

value.definition: Requirements are the constitutional WHAT: invariant truths and stable obligations the project must make true, including capabilities, constraints, guarantees, governance and verification. They carry explicit acceptance criteria and sufficient lifecycle obligations or named ambiguity gaps for downstream design.

grounding.quote:
Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true.

value.label: Requirements

value.definition: Design is structural HOW: decisions, interfaces, topology, carrier surfaces, file placement, entry/control surfaces, runtime wiring and lawful tenant boundaries that realise requirement truth. ADRs are durable design records and memory, not an additional constitutional layer or requirement surface.

grounding.quote:
Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design.

value.label: Design and ADRs

value.definition: Realisation carries design decisions as software code, performed human procedure or both according to its execution binding. value.definition: F11 explains change entry, computed classification and reuse, ambiguity governance, and shared-interface migration. This family (F11 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides how a change enters the chain, how its classification is computed
and reused, how ambiguity is governed and how a shared interface is
migrated. Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are
named in the rows as follows: changing specification, the specification
changes while work proceeds; one front door, reports of every kind arrive
at one product; shared interfaces, a shared interface has several
producers and consumers; reserved decisions, a decision may be taken
under declared policy or be reserved to a human authority. Standing of
the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and
P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that
step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5 derived from P0 and P6,

a defective realisation, an inadequate governing requirement or design, an

value.definition: The intake-triage declaration of where a change lawfully re-enters the constitutional chain, using SPEC_METHOD §4 classes. Common, nonexclusive pairings are feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor. A spike remains exploratory while carrying its current triage class.

grounding.quote:
Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of
work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully
re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`
declared by intake triage, using the classes of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) (P4b, P2; rc.2
#change-class).

value.label: Ticket change class

value.definition: A source-described triage operation consuming computed classification for owner/layer traversal, complete relevant public membership and value delta, accepted-design scope, trace coverage and rule-determined treatment. For bugs it walks upward from the realised surface and associates the highest missing or insufficient governing layer with its lawful re-entry class.

grounding.quote:
Triage consumes the computed classification of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment) for
the declared owner and layer traversal, the complete relevant public
membership and value delta, the accepted-design scope and trace coverage,
and the rule-determined treatment. The owning work carrier references that
exact result and its residuals; a new role does not repeat an unchanged
walk (P4b, P2; rc.2 #upward-propagation-check).

value.label: Upward propagation check

value.definition: The minimum ticket status population is backlog, active and completed. Ticket/local statuses, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and recorded change_class are declared carrier states, not evaluation results. Backlog is accepted durable work outside current focus; active is the bounded execution set; completed is closed historical work.

grounding.quote:
The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes).

`backlog`
is accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part of the
current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

value.label: Declared work-carrier states and lanes

value.definition: One run-scoped contract for every execution governed by the described method. The smallest lawful source carrier is selected by required lifetime after establishing upstream work authority: an exact admitted ticket, durable ticket, admitted sprint with manifest-local iteration, or intake-drafted run contract. Ticket-shaped means required categorisation, closure criteria, proof, non-closure conditions and fields, without creating ticket identity or lane state.

grounding.quote:
Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside
an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it
is the current run (P2, P4b, P6; rc.2 #work-carrier-to-execution-rule).

value.label: Run-scoped execution contract

value.definition: F13 explains work-carrier rules through stated commitments and instance premises: lifetimes, several apparent work-state surfaces, several tenants, migrations and variable carrier forms. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are independent where cited; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. The table distinguishes consequences, member policy, external ownership and consumers; §10 records dispositions and decides nothing.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises, which the commitments do
not supply, are named in the rows as follows: lifetimes, work and its
obligations last one run, one bounded batch or longer; several surfaces,
goals, tickets, comments, boards and summaries can each appear to state
the same work state; several tenants, one work item may be realised in
more than one build tenant; migrations, some work replaces one
authoritative truth path with another across producers, consumers and
proofs; carriers vary, a project may keep its carriers in files, trackers
or services.

value.label: F13 work-carrier foundation-to-law account

value.definition: The table's eleven consumer routes respectively concern: lifetime selection and carrier binding (SPEC_METHOD, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, CONFORMANCE 41, judgment continuity); admitted execution (ACTIVATION, ODD); authority/projections (PRODUCT_DEFINITION, recommended shapes); sprint batching (SPEC_METHOD, UX, CONFORMANCE 48, status, closure and manifest); triage (SPEC_METHOD, sprint admission, carrier selection and ticket shape); tenant lifecycles (SPEC_METHOD §11, PRODUCT_DEFINITION); migration (DESIGN_MODULE, status and migration shape); assessment/rulings (EVALUATION, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, computed classification, recurrence); closure/tests (SPEC_METHOD consistency/evidence, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, ASSURANCE, milestones); term binding (internal admission/closure only); carrier shapes/reading (no separate consumer). Consumers apply owning rules without adding decisions.

grounding.quote:
Consumers of these rows, where an actor enters them (FOUNDATIONS §3
Foundation to law, Consumers), one list per row, each consumer linked to
its own locus:

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

value.label: Work-carrier consumer routes

value.definition: Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis without admitting that basis. Contract states include drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded. Basis admission or renewal belongs to the selected goals-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and remains durably legible in existing goals or ticket authority.

grounding.quote:
Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome,
prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis (ACTIVATION
§1). Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the
selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and stays
durably legible in the existing goals or ticket authority

value.label: Contract admission distinct from basis admission

value.definition: Evaluation criteria identify progress/completion, while non-closure conditions identify continuing failure despite local green proof; together they are the work's local gain function.

grounding.quote:
An execution contract should expose both what counts as progress or
completion and what still counts as failure even when some local proof is
green. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and
`non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for
the work

value.label: Evaluation and non-closure conditions

value.definition: Ticket and work-instruction terms are resolved under PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 using the cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis, affected scope and any authorised semantic relation.

grounding.quote:
Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning

value.label: Bounded-context term binding

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration
value.definition: A ticket-local authority surface containing an explicit migration declaration and live Markdown checklist. The declaration names strategy, exact affected scope, every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope and deterministic routing, old/new truth paths or contracts, both old/new producer and consumer sets, every derived projection/report/status/proof surface, and migration closure law.

grounding.quote:
The declaration states: the migration strategy used for this work item; the
exact affected migration scope; every explicitly excluded or disjoint
product or compatibility scope with its deterministic routing relation; the
old truth path or superseded contract; the new truth path or authoritative
contract; the producer set for the old and the new path; the consumer set
for the old and the new path; every projection, report, status surface and
proof surface derived from that contract family; and the closure law for
the migration.

value.label: Implementation migration ticket

value.definition: Upstream migration tickets publish or admit the new authoritative source carrier. Downstream tickets harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review surfaces and other consumers. Their authored dependency chain runs source carrier to downstream consumers.

grounding.quote:
When one migration
wave introduces a new source carrier and then its prompt, projection or
read-model consumers, the dependency chain runs `source carrier ->
downstream consumers`, never the reverse.

value.label: Migration source-carrier ticket

value.definition: Migration work on consumers downstream of the source-carrier ticket, including prompt, projection, read-model and review surfaces.

grounding.quote:
Tickets that harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review
surfaces or other downstream consumers depend on those upstream source
tickets.

value.label: Downstream migration ticket

value.definition: Migration strategy values are inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption. Library-use values are none, consume and extend, distinguishing local rebuilding, consumption and extension of a reusable library/commonisation surface before local implementation lands.

grounding.quote:
The required fields are `migration_strategy`, with the values
`inside_out_hard_break` and `fundamental_re_adoption`, and
`library_usage`, with the values `none`, `consume` and `extend`.

An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local
implementation lands; `library_usage` records which

value.label: Migration strategy and library-use domains

value.definition: A ticket-specific review surface for functional migration questions, a named interface-by-interface closure checklist, ordered breaks and break-to-closure mappings. These are described review operations and document roles, not performed reviews.

grounding.quote:
For a core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration, the
ticket includes an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be
used as closure evidence. The checklist is a named walk of every live
interface that can still bypass, reinterpret, replay or project the
migrating truth path

value.label: Migration review and execution documents

value.definition: Independent assessment is distinct from authoring, self-review and the decision owner's acceptance. Tier-1 assessment/acceptance laws are cited to EVALUATION §§3,5 and closed-result reuse to ACTIVATION §7; this member specifies their work-carrier consequences.

grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).
This section states what those laws require of work carriers.

value.label: Independent assessment and acceptance distinction

value.definition: Reusable records in the owning work carrier: residual judgment J carries its question, exact subject/basis, computed facts/evidence, actor/authority, conclusion/scope, uncertainty and concrete revising observation; owner ruling O carries original wording, owner, subject/basis, permitted scope/effects, conditions and source separately from agent interpretation. C, J and O are source annotations, not newly instantiated judgment populations.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5. The record
identifies the question; the exact subject and governing basis; the
supporting computed facts and evidence; the responsible actor and its
authority; the conclusion and its scope; the uncertainty; and a concrete
revising observation that lets a consumer determine whether the conclusion
still applies.

value.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

value.definition: Retained, superseded, deferred and withdrawn are obligation states set by the owning authority after repricing, with evidence links. They accept no candidate and map to no core value; they differ from assessed-candidate acceptance dispositions and predecessor-claim dispositions evaluated by qualification.

grounding.quote:
The four repricing dispositions are recorded states of the obligation,
set by its owning authority; they are not results and map to no core
value.

value.label: Obligation repricing states

value.definition: A work claim closes by the conjunction of its applicable declared obligations, valid exact-scope evidence, required applicable judgments/rulings and absence of active non-closure conditions. This section owns the condition applied by SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate.

grounding.quote:
This condition is the
[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the
closure condition of a work claim;
[SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate](SPEC_METHOD.md#consistency-gate)
applies it as the gate over a declared change span.

value.label: Condition-based work-claim closure

value.definition: Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority. The recommended derivation for every substantive test is ticket → intake triage → lawful re-entry → governing requirement/design/module/published function/carrier/closure surface → test expectation.

grounding.quote:
ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation

value.label: Test authority and expectations

value.definition: One work-state authority chain assigns the bounded wave to goals, ticket state to the ticket, subordinate milestone state to milestone authority, and realisation decisions to accepted design. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections.

grounding.quote:
Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections

value.label: Work-state authority and projections

Markdown titles supply descriptive headings, and the examples carry fields, authority/context, scope/acceptance and links or migration declaration/checklist.

An implementation migration ticket, carrying the declaration, fields and

conditions: The default local-file carrier is used.
value.definition: Humans and agents read active files directly; backlog stays durably searchable outside immediate focus; rg suffices for finding active work; neither database nor board is required. The sample commands search headings/status/type/goal in active or backlog folders and ticket IDs across tickets.

grounding.quote:
The default local-file carrier assumes that humans and agents can read the
active ticket folder directly; that backlog remains searchable durable work
without competing with the active lane for immediate attention; that `rg`
is sufficient for finding active work; and that no database or board is
required

value.label: Default local-file operating mode

value.definition: Surface roles are separated: goals identify the current broad wave; SPEC_METHOD supplies constitutional change class/re-entry; sprints price a bounded batch's proof/evidence/paydown; tickets identify durable work and state; comments record proposals, arguments, decisions, reviews and handoffs; POSTING_GUIDE specifies comment publication structure/naming. This avoids goals as overloaded backlog, deferred work diluting active focus, comments as informal task status, or boards as accidental authority.

grounding.quote:
The goals surface: what broad work wave
matters now. SPEC_METHOD: what constitutional change class and re-entry
point govern the work. Sprints: what bounded execution batch is currently
pricing proof, evidence and paydown. Tickets: what durable units of work
exist and what state they are in. Comments: what was proposed, argued,
decided, reviewed or handed off. POSTING_GUIDE: how comment-layer
publications are structured and named.

value.label: Relationships among work surfaces

grounding.quote:
A Markov object is
a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure whose internal
state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket. The term is
substrate-neutral: the same topology is expected wherever a constraint
structure admits stable configurations, in biological systems (Friston's
original setting), in the natural-language traces those systems emit, in
learned representations built over those traces (LLMs), and in the
engineered institutional systems descended from both. The working claim
is that world-model construction is possible because this topology
propagates across substrates: what domain experts recognise as "objects"
in an institutional system is the same kind of structure Friston
described for biological systems, re-expressed through another
substrate. The profile is the practice of making that structure explicit,
traceable and publishable (P3, P6).
